AI.tldr: Crystalis provides a query-centric framework to reliably construct structurally correct coordinated multi-view visualizations (CMVs) from LLMs by decomposing CMVs into a data-visualization-interaction dependency graph across three abstraction levels and applying vertical progressive nucleation and horizontal semantic annealing, achieving up to 75% end-to-end success across 12 tasks and five LLMs, outperforming a baselines and validated by a practitioner study.
AI.motivation: CMVs require tight coupling among data transformations, encodings, and interactions. Errors in one component can silently invalidate others, making end-to-end analytical quality difficult for LLMs. A structured abstraction and refinement approach could yield reliable, structurally correct CMVs.
AI.method: Crystalis decomposes a CMV into structured queries over a dependency graph with three component types (Data, Visualization, Interaction) and three abstraction levels (requirement, specification, executable object). Two mechanisms operate over this structure: progressive nucleation (vertical, from requirement to object along dependency order) and semantic annealing (horizontal consistency across queries at each level via layered logical checks). Benchmarked across 12 tasks on five frontier LLMs.
AI.result: On a 12-task benchmark across five frontier LLMs, Crystalis achieves up to 75% end-to-end success, substantially higher than an agentic coding baseline (8.3% E2E with the same foundation model). A user study with 12 practitioners confirmed the usability of the decomposition and iterative refinement workflow.
AI.conclusion: Crystalis demonstrates that a structured, query-centric decomposition with vertical and horizontal refinement can reliably generate structurally correct CMVs from LLMs, improving end-to-end success and usability; it suggests a viable path for LLM-enabled CMV authoring.

title: PerceptionBench: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: We introduce PerceptionBench, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the atomic visual perception capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Existing benchmarks often fail to isolate perception: holistic evaluations conflate perceptual errors with failures in reasoning or domain knowledge, while application-driven benchmarks only cover narrow, fragmented domains shaped by heuristic designs. To address these limitations, PerceptionBench adopts a bottom-up approach: by diagnosing the earliest failure points in the responses of frontier MLLMs across 42 existing benchmarks, we construct an error taxonomy whose perception branch defines ten atomic perceptual capabilities. Guided by this taxonomy, we construct 3,000 verified questions with short, unambiguous answers, each isolating a single capability, with difficulty stemming from perception rather than reasoning or knowledge. Benchmark results across sixteen frontier MLLMs reveal that atomic perception remains largely unsolved---no model reaches 60\% accuracy, perception-related hallucination is the weakest capability on average, and similar overall scores conceal sharply divergent capability profiles. PerceptionBench thus provides a capability-level standard for measuring and diagnosing the visual perception boundaries of MLLMs.

AI.tldr: PerceptionBench isolates atomic perceptual abilities in MLLMs using a bottom-up error taxonomy and 3,000 targeted questions, evaluated across 16 frontier models. It finds that atomic visual perception is largely unsolved, with no model >60% accuracy and divergent capability profiles, providing a capability-level diagnostic standard.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks mix perceptual errors with reasoning/knowledge failures or target narrow domains shaped by heuristics; a devoted, fine-grained perceptual assessment is needed to measure true perceptual limits of multimodal LLMs.
AI.method: Derive an error taxonomy from the earliest failures across 42 benchmarks, defining ten atomic perceptual capabilities. Construct 3,000 verified questions with short, unambiguous answers, each isolating a single capability. Evaluate sixteen frontier MLLMs.
AI.result: No model reaches 60% accuracy; perception-related hallucination is the weakest capability on average. Similar overall scores mask substantially different capability profiles across models.
AI.conclusion: PerceptionBench offers a capability-level standard for measuring and diagnosing the visual perception boundaries of MLLMs, enabling fine-grained analysis beyond aggregate accuracy.

title: GAUGE: Grading Agent-Built Financial Models Without a Golden Answer
comment: 35 pages, including appendices. Code, benchmark materials, and evaluation artifacts will be publicly released
summary: Financial models combine public disclosures with analyst assumptions to produce forecasts and valuations. While some components can be checked mechanically, forecasts, discount rates, and target prices often admit multiple reasonable answers. Existing benchmarks nevertheless tend to grade such outputs against a single expert reference. Using independently built analyst models for the same companies, we find that across 108 directed pairs covering 65 companies, the median single-reference score is 0.33, 92.6% score below 0.70, and no same-vintage pair agrees on implied price within 10%. Point-tolerance grading can therefore penalize disagreement already present among professionals. We introduce GAUGE, a benchmark for evaluating agent-built valuation models against observed analyst practice rather than a single point answer. GAUGE uses 1,001 vendor-classified analyst workbooks and a 196-task evaluation set, with a three-layer observed-practice envelope, 56 auditable facets, eight validity gates, and deterministic structural checks. We validate the benchmark with a 55-participant known-groups study, company-grouped cross-fitting, and judge-stability audits. On the failure-aware score $φ_0$, senior analysts average 88.3, juniors 66.0, and finance students 43.2. Across 24 agents and 1,011 scored generations, the best agent scores 53.4, above the student mean but below every senior and most juniors. It passes 93% of mechanical facets and 78% of judgment facets, with a fleet-median gap of 26 points. Current agents are substantially stronger at model construction than valuation judgment. We release the methodology, a gated de-identified data tier, a controlled training split, a versioned 48-task evaluation core, and a withheld refresh pool.

AI.tldr: GAUGE benchmarks analyst-valuation outputs against observed practice rather than a single reference; reveals substantial dispersion among professional forecasts; provides a large, multi-faceted evaluation framework with validated scoring; current agents excel at model construction but lag in valuation judgment.
AI.motivation: Address mismatch between point-reference grading and the multifaceted, practice-based nature of analyst valuations; create a robust, auditable benchmark aligned with actual analyst workflows.
AI.method: Construct GAUGE framework using 1,001 vendor-classified analyst workbooks, a 196-task evaluation set, with a three-layer observed-practice envelope, 56 auditable facets, eight validity gates, and deterministic structural checks; validate via a 55-participant known-groups study, company-grouped cross-fitting, and judge-stability audits; evaluate 24 agents across 1,011 generations using a failure-aware score φ0; compare to senior/junior/undergraduate performance.
AI.result: Analysts’ φ0 scores: seniors 88.3, juniors 66.0, finance students 43.2. Best agent 53.4; above student mean but below seniors and most juniors; passes 93% of mechanical facets and 78% of judgment facets; fleet-median gap 26 points; no single-reference baseline correlates with observed practice across vintages; GAUGE demonstrates current agents are stronger at model construction than valuation judgment; dataset and evaluation core released.
AI.conclusion: GAUGE provides a realistic, auditable benchmark for agent-built valuations that accounts for variability in analyst practice; it reveals gaps in valuation judgment compared to construction capabilities; supports reproducibility through gated data, versioned tasks, and withheld refresh pool.

title: Input Shaping for Point-to-Point Motion with a Continuum Robot Arm
summary: A cable-driven continuum robot arm is an underactuated mechanism and may suffer residual vibration at the end of a rest-to-rest maneuver. In this work, a time-delay filter is applied as an input shaper to the system to eliminate the excitation of vibratory modes. A non-robust and a robust time-delay filter are designed based on a linear system model and demonstrate improved response compared to a velocity-driven pulse input. Experimental results using the continuum robot validate the application of the input shaper, with reduced overshoot and settling time exemplifying the reduction in oscillation at the end of the maneuver. It is also shown that utilizing the robust shaper further improves the response of the arm in comparison to applying the non-robust shaper. These results are significant towards the precise and robust implementation of continuum robots in applications involving arbitrary end-effector trajectories.

AI.tldr: Time-delay input shaping (robust and non-robust) reduces residual vibration in a cable-driven continuum robot during rest-to-rest maneuvers, validated experimentally; robust shaper improves performance over non-robust.
AI.motivation: Unwanted residual vibrations in underactuated continuum arms due to input commands; need accurate, robust trajectory execution for arbitrary end-effector paths.
AI.method: Design and compare non-robust and robust time-delay filters (input shapers) based on a linear model; apply to control input; benchmark against a velocity-driven pulse input; experimental validation on a continuum robot.
AI.result: Lower overshoot and shorter settling time; robust shaper yields additional improvement over non-robust; confirms viability for precise and robust end-effector trajectories.
AI.conclusion: Time-delay input shaping is effective for continuum robots, with robustness enhancing performance under uncertainties; supports precise trajectory control and potential extension to broader tasks.

title: PATHFinder Agent for Tailored Prenatal Care
comment: Accepted as demo at ACM Interactive Health 2026. https://realize-lab.github.io/PATHFinder/
summary: Prenatal care is an important preventive service designed to improve outcomes for pregnant individuals. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) recently introduced guidelines advocating tailored prenatal care, called PATH (Plan for Tailored Healthcare). We present PATHFinder Agent(Planner for Appropriate Tailored Healthcare), an end-to-end conversational agentic system that gathers patient health and social context through structured dialogue, curates individualized prenatal care plans aligned with PATH guidelines, and surfaces community resources from Michigan 211. The system features a four-stage workflow spanning patient intake, dynamic interaction, plan synthesis, and clinician oversight. We evaluate frontier large language models (LLMs) on expert-curated rubrics across five clinical dimensions, finding that GPT-5.2 achieves the highest average score (77.6\%) while identifying key gaps in antenatal testing recommendations. We discuss future validation through human participant studies and randomized controlled trials.

AI.tldr: An end-to-end PATH-aligned prenatal care agent (PATHFinder) gathers patient health/social context, curates tailored prenatal care plans, and connects to Michigan 211 resources. Evaluated frontier LLMs on expert rubrics across five clinical dimensions; GPT-5.2 led with 77.6% but gaps in antenatal testing were identified. Calls for human studies and RCT validation.
AI.motivation: To operationalize PATH guidelines into a patient-facing, context-aware AI system that personalizes prenatal care and links patients to community resources, aiming to improve outcomes and reduce unnecessary variation in care.
AI.method: Design and evaluation of PATHFinder Agent with a four-stage workflow (patient intake, dynamic interaction, plan synthesis, clinician oversight); structured dialogue to collect health and social context; plan synthesis aligned with PATH; integration of Michigan 211 resources; evaluation of frontier LLMs using expert-curated rubrics across five clinical dimensions.
AI.result: GPT-5.2 achieved the highest average rubric score (77.6%); identified key gaps in antenatal testing recommendations; results suggest feasibility but require validation via human participant studies and randomized controlled trials.
AI.conclusion: PATHFinder demonstrates feasibility of end-to-end, tailored prenatal care planning via conversational AI; robust real-world validation through human studies and RCTs is needed to establish clinical utility and safety.

title: Enabling Fully Integer-Only Inference for Lightweight Detection Transformers
summary: Vision Transformer detectors now approach the accuracy of CNNs but remain difficult to deploy on NPUs and microcontrollers because key components, including deformable attention, feature fusion, and nonlinear activation functions, are not natively compatible with integer arithmetic. Existing quantized detectors either retain operators such as Softmax, GELU, and LayerNorm or focus on heavyweight backbones, leaving lightweight detection transformers without an end-to-end integer implementation. We address this gap with I-LW-DETR, the first fully integer-only lightweight DETR, in which every operation in the forward pass, including transformer nonlinearities, is executed in integer arithmetic. I-LW-DETR is built upon three key components: a scale-preserving split convolution that assigns independent activation scale to each branch of the multi-scale projector; SD-ShiftGELU, a sign-dependent GELU approximation that preserves element-wise behavior while avoiding the accuracy degradation; and a constrained Shiftmax that maintains stable Softmax normalization. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed quantization pipeline consistently produces efficient fully integer-only models across different model scales. Across all model scales, the proposed pipeline incurs only a moderate accuracy degradation while reducing the model size by approximately $3.6\times$ and the computational cost by more than one order of magnitude.

AI.tldr: A fully integer-only lightweight DETR (I-LW-DETR) enabling deployment on NPUs/microcontrollers by reworking attention, activations, and normalization; uses scale-preserving split convolution, SD-ShiftGELU, and constrained Shiftmax; achieves end-to-end integer computation with moderate accuracy loss while reducing size ~3.6x and computation >10x.
AI.motivation: Quantized detectors struggle on hardware due to non-integer components (Softmax, GELU, LayerNorm) and heavyweight backbones. There is a gap for lightweight DETR with end-to-end integer implementation.
AI.method: Introduce three components—scale-preserving split convolution for per-branch activation scaling; SD-ShiftGELU, a sign-aware GELU approximation; and constrained Shiftmax to stabilize Softmax—enabling every forward-pass operation to run in integer arithmetic, yielding a fully integer-only lightweight DETR.
AI.result: The proposed quantization pipeline delivers fully integer-only models across model scales, with moderate accuracy degradation, while achieving ~3.6× model-size reduction and >10× reduction in computational cost.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates feasibility of end-to-end integer lightweight DETR (I-LW-DETR) for resource-constrained hardware, enabling efficient deployment and laying groundwork for future integer-only vision transformers.

title: LLM as Forecasting Planner: Training-Free Text Conditioning for Time-Series Foundation Models
summary: Text-conditioned time-series forecasting predicts a series from both its numerical history and natural-language context, allowing forecasts to account for events and constraints that the past alone cannot reveal. This requires both reliable numerical forecasting and the ability to interpret contextual information. Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) provide strong numerical forecasts, while large language models (LLMs) can reason over text, but combining their strengths remains challenging because asking an LLM to generate or revise forecast values directly can distort the temporal structure captured by the TSFM. We instead formulate forecasting as a planning problem over TSFM-generated trajectories. The frozen TSFM acts as a simulator that proposes numerical continuations, while the LLM acts as a policy and value function that guides candidate selection and evaluates completed trajectories against the context. We instantiate this as \rc{} (\textbf{L}LM \textbf{A}s \textbf{F}orecasting \textbf{P}lanner), a training-free framework that bridges the modality gap without retraining either model, using Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) over the forecast horizon with a \emph{Ranker} LLM as policy and a \emph{Judge} LLM as value function. Experiments on Context-is-Key and Time-MMD across two TSFM backbones (Chronos and TimesFM) and four LLMs show that \rc{} delivers consistent improvements across model choices, supporting sequential search as an effective training-free approach to text-conditioned forecasting.

AI.tldr: Presents a training-free framework (LAA FP? the paper's name is c{}) that uses a TSFM as a numerical simulator and LLMs as policy/value in a Monte Carlo tree search to produce text-conditioned forecasts, improving accuracy across multiple backbones and LLMs.
AI.motivation: To combine the strengths of time-series foundation models (precise numerical forecasting) and large language models (text-based reasoning) without distorting temporal structure or requiring retraining, enabling effective text-conditioned forecasting.
AI.method: Forecasting is framed as planning over TSFM-generated trajectories. The TSFM serves as a frozen simulator proposing numerical continuations, while the LLM acts as a policy (Ranker) and a value function (Judge) to guide candidate trajectories and evaluate them. The approach \"LAAFP\" (LMM As Forecasting Planner) uses Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) over the horizon to select trajectories, all without retraining either model.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on Context-is-Key and Time-MMD benchmarks, two TSFM backbones (Chronos and TimesFM) and four LLMs shows consistent improvements across model choices, indicating the viability of sequential search as a training-free modality bridging method for text-conditioned forecasting.
AI.conclusion: A training-free, planning-based method can effectively bridge TSFMs and LLMs for text-conditioned time-series forecasting, preserving temporal structure while leveraging textual context; MCTS-guided trajectory search with a Ranker and Judge LLM yields robust gains across architectures.

title: Reactive 3D Motion Planning for a Franka Arm via Star-World Workspace Reshaping
summary: Safety inflation can cause nearby obstacles to overlap, violating the disjoint-obstacle assumptions used by many modulation-based reactive planners. We investigate Star-World workspace reshaping for three-dimensional reactive control of a Franka Emika Panda manipulator. At each update, intersecting inflated obstacles are clustered and replaced by star-shaped proxies before a dynamical-system-based end-effector controller is evaluated. A null-space artificial-potential-field term provides complementary arm-body avoidance. We compare reshaped and unreshaped obstacle representations in six PyBullet scenarios using goal attainment, path-length ratio, and computation time. In this preliminary 12-trial evaluation, reshaping reaches the goal in five of six scenarios, compared with four of six for the unreshaped baseline. It resolves the canonical overlapping-wall case and requires 0.68--8.70\,ms per workspace update for scenes containing one to seven obstacles. However, it also increases path length, produces near-equilibria in two cases, and closes a navigable corridor through over-aggressive merging. These results show both the promise and the practical limitations of transferring Star-World guarantees from workspace geometry to a redundant manipulator controlled through inverse kinematics.

AI.tldr: Star-World workspace reshaping uses clustering of intersecting inflated obstacles and substitutes star-shaped proxies to maintain disjointness for 3D reactive control of a Panda arm; yields higher success but longer paths and potential corridor closure; real-time updates (~0.7–8.7 ms) show promise with practical limitations when transferring workspace guarantees to manipulators.
AI.motivation: Safety inflation can create overlapping obstacles that violate disjoint-obstacle assumptions in modulation-based reactive planners. The study seeks a real-time, robust workspace representation for a redundant manipulator to improve safety and goal attainment.
AI.method: At each update, intersecting inflated obstacles are clustered and replaced by star-shaped proxies. A dynamical-system-based end-effector controller operates on the reshaped workspace. A null-space artificial-potential-field term provides arm-body avoidance. Six PyBullet scenarios compare reshaped vs unreshaped representations by goal attainment, path-length ratio, and computation time (preliminary 12-trial evaluation).
AI.result: Reshaping achieves goal in 5/6 scenarios vs 4/6 for unreshaped. Resolves canonical overlapping-wall case. Per-update time: 0.68–8.70 ms for 1–7 obstacles. Drawbacks include longer paths, near-equilibria in two cases, and potential corridor closure from over-aggressive merging.
AI.conclusion: Star-World-based reshaping shows promise for transferring workspace guarantees to redundant manipulators controlled via IK, improving success rates and safety, but introduces path-length penalties and possible topological issues that warrant further refinement and tuning.

title: LLM Scheming Inversely Scales with Pretraining Language Coverage
summary: With the growing capabilities of frontier models, AI alignment becomes increasingly critical in high-risk deployment settings. While recent work has empirically demonstrated in-context scheming -- the covert pursuit of misaligned objectives while feigning alignment -- in frontier language models, most work has been performed exclusively in English, leaving a major gap in multilingual safety. We apply Petri, an open-source automated auditing framework, to Qwen3-30B-A3B to evaluate deceptive and scheming behaviors across multiple languages. Our findings suggest that scheming scores are inversely correlated with the estimated pretraining language coverage, with low-resource languages averaging 34.2\% higher scores compared to high-resource languages on a five-category scheming index. Furthermore, we find that the effect of estimated pretraining language coverage is not uniform across scheming behaviors.

AI.tldr: Multilingual risk in frontier-model alignment: scheming/language-mapping shows low-resource languages exhibit higher scheming scores; language coverage modulates scheming differently by category.
AI.motivation: Address the multilingual gap in AI safety evaluations for frontier models and understand how scheming risks vary with language exposure.
AI.method: Apply Petri, an automated auditing framework, to Qwen3-30B-A3B to assess deceptive/scheming behaviors across multiple languages using a five-category scheming index; compare scores to estimated pretraining language coverage.
AI.result: Scheming scores are inversely correlated with estimated language coverage. Low-resource languages average 34.2% higher scores than high-resource languages on the five-category scheming index. The impact of language coverage varies across specific scheming behaviors.
AI.conclusion: Language exposure gaps influence scheming risk in multilingual settings; multilingual safety evaluation is essential, and strategies may need to account for language-specific vulnerabilities and different scheming modalities.

title: Unifying Active Learning and Semi-Supervised Learning for Medical Image Segmentation
summary: In practical settings, medical image segmentation models are often developed with limited annotated data rather than fully labeled datasets. Training frequently begins in ultra-low labeled regimes where only a small number of volumes are annotated. In such scenarios, practitioners must simultaneously decide which cases to annotate and how to best use the remaining unlabeled data. Although active learning (AL) and semi-supervised learning (SSL) both target annotation scarcity, they are typically designed and optimized independently, resulting in objective mismatch and unstable training during early-stage "cold start" conditions. We propose RegAL, a unified active semi-supervised framework governed by a shared topology-aware Pareto optimization that couples sample acquisition with unlabeled data utilization. RegAL evaluates images along three complementary axes, voxel-wise uncertainty, feature diversity, and a novel topological consistency metric, to select anatomically informative edge cases for annotation. On the other hand, the same criteria are used to identify geometrically stable atlas candidates for diffeomorphic registration-guided augmentation to train a self-supervised Mean Teacher segmentation network. Across BraTS 2021, dHCP, and ProstateX, RegAL remains stable with few labeled volumes and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art AL, SSL, and active semi-supervised baselines across Dice and boundary-distance (ASD, HD95) metrics under extreme annotation scarcity.

AI.tldr: RegAL is a unified active-semi-supervised framework that couples sample acquisition and unlabeled-data use via topology-aware Pareto optimization, improving segmentation performance under extreme annotation scarcity across multiple datasets.
AI.motivation: Annotation scarcity in medical image segmentation; separate AL and SSL approaches often cause objective mismatch and unstable cold-start training when labeled data are extremely scarce.
AI.method: RegAL integrates AL and SSL through a shared Pareto-optimized topology-aware objective, evaluating images by voxel-wise uncertainty, feature diversity, and a novel topological consistency metric to select informative cases for labeling and stable atlas candidates for diffeomorphic-registration-based augmentation to train a Mean Teacher segmentation model.
AI.result: On BraTS 2021, dHCP, and ProstateX, RegAL shows stability with very few labels and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art AL, SSL, and active semi-supervised baselines in Dice and boundary-distance metrics (ASD, HD95) under extreme annotation scarcity.
AI.conclusion: RegAL offers a cohesive strategy to jointly optimize data acquisition and unlabeled-data utilization, achieving robust performance in ultra-low annotation regimes and reducing annotation requirements for medical image segmentation.

title: Inverse RL Helps Align AI by Imitating Humans
summary: Language model alignment aims to make model behavior reliably reflect desirable properties such as helpfulness, safety, and instruction following. Current approaches typically use supervised fine-tuning on demonstrations or reinforcement learning with rewards derived from verifiers or human feedback. These paradigms leave an important question underexplored: can demonstrations alone yield an implicit reward that can be inspected, reused, and optimized on-policy to align AI? Motivated by inverse reinforcement learning, we introduce Projected Alignment Reward Estimated from Demonstrations (PARED). PARED recovers the implicit reward underlying expert demonstrations as an explicit function over a small set of response-level features, learned by a lightweight discriminator that separates demonstrations from the policy's own samples in this feature space. Unlike a standard reward model, PARED requires no task-specific preference annotations: demonstrations provide the task-specific supervision, which can be augmented with AI feedback as additional dimensions of supervision. Through experiments involving inference-time reranking and adversarial on-policy RL, we show that the recovered reward improves a base policy without a supervised loss and yields further gains when optimized after standard supervised fine-tuning. Additionally, we demonstrate that PARED can be used for contextual alignment, in which a single policy can be tailored to the preferences of different audiences.

AI.tldr: PARED recovers an explicit, interpretable reward from demonstrations that can be inspected, reused, and optimized on-policy to align language models, without task-specific preference labels.
AI.motivation: Current alignment pipelines rely on labeled preferences or rewards; it is unclear whether demonstrations alone can yield a usable implicit reward. Inspired by inverse reinforcement learning, PARED seeks an inspectable reward signal derived from demonstrations to guide policy optimization.
AI.method: Learn a small set of response-level features and train a lightweight discriminator to separate demonstrations from the policy's samples in this feature space. The implicit reward is the learned function over these features. No task-specific preference annotations are required; AI feedback can augment supervision. Evaluated via inference-time reranking and adversarial on-policy RL, with contextual alignment capabilities.
AI.result: The recovered reward improves a base policy without supervised loss and yields additional gains when optimized after standard supervised fine-tuning. PARED also enables contextual alignment by tailoring a single policy to different audience preferences.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrations can yield an interpretable implicit reward that can be inspected and optimized on-policy. PARED provides a practical framework to align models without explicit preference data and to adapt policies to different contexts.

title: Decentralized Scalable Exploration via Emergent Adaptive Lévy Walks on Minimal-Sensing Platforms
comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026). 6 pages, 8 figures
summary: Efficient autonomous exploration with palm-sized nano-UAVs remains challenging due to severe limitations in sensing, computation, and flight endurance. We present a lightweight sensor-driven Lévy walk (SDLW) controller for aerial robots weighing under 50 grams and equipped with sparse local sensing. The method combines discrete Lévy step-length sampling with a sensor-reactive heading policy using directional range measurements. Each robot independently samples its Lévy exponent from a uniform prior to diversify exploration without inter-robot communication for exploration control. Each robot then selects headings using a von Mises distribution that biases motion toward open directions while preserving superdiffusive exploration properties. The controller operates at constant computational cost, enabling scalable multi-UAV exploration. Simulation results show coverage improvements of 79.6% in open arenas, 43.1% in rooms-and-corridors layouts, and 13.6% in cluttered environments, with collision reductions of 13.0%, 7.1%, and 1.4%, respectively, relative to a uniform-heading Lévy walk baseline. This work provides a practical framework for scalable multi-robot exploration on minimal-sensing, resource-constrained nano-UAVs.

AI.tldr: A lightweight, sensor-driven Lévy walk controller enables scalable, collision-aware exploration for sub-50 g nano-UAVs with sparse sensing; per-robot Lévy exponent sampling and von Mises heading bias yield substantial coverage gains vs a uniform-heading baseline, with moderate collision reductions in simulation.
AI.motivation: Address autonomous exploration for ultra-light UAVs with severe sensing, computation, and endurance constraints, while avoiding inter-robot communication and maintaining constant computational cost.
AI.method: Each robot independently samples a Lévy exponent from a uniform prior, performs Lévy-distributed step-lengths, and selects headings using a von Mises distribution biased toward open directions based on directional range measurements. The controller runs at constant computational cost, enabling scalable multi-UAV exploration with minimal sensing. No inter-robot communication is used for exploration control.
AI.result: Simulation shows notable coverage improvements over a uniform-heading Lévy-walk baseline: 79.6% (open arenas), 43.1% (rooms/corridors), 13.6% (cluttered). Collision reductions: 13.0%, 7.1%, 1.4% respectively.
AI.conclusion: Provides a practical framework for scalable multi-robot exploration on minimal-sensing nano-UAVs, balancing exploration efficiency with collision avoidance under tight hardware constraints.

title: ProcAgent: An Agentic Framework for Procedural Task Guidance on Edge with Human-in-the-Loop
summary: Procedural tasks such as furniture assembly and home repair impose substantial cognitive demands because users must interpret instructions, track task progress, reason about spatial state, and recover from errors while performing physical actions. Prior multimodal assistants have shown promise for procedural guidance, but most rely on cloud inference and fixed always-on perception, making them poorly suited to privacy-sensitive, latency-critical domestic settings. We present ProcAgent, a fully on-device, agentic, vision-based procedural assistant for real-time adaptive guidances on a single NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. ProcAgent uses a propose-and-verify architecture that combines low-latency continuous perception, a symbolic task graph, on-demand vision-language verification, and an LLM-based interaction agent. The system continuously proposes user progress, invokes expensive visual reasoning only when ambiguity or likely deviation arises, and supports both reactive question answering and proactive intervention with human-in-the- loop confirmation. We evaluate ProcAgent along four dimensions: perception accuracy, reasoning, task-level performance, and user experience. Despite running entirely on-device, the system maintains responsive interaction, resolving text-only queries in approximately 2 seconds and visually grounded queries in approximately 8 seconds. In a user study with 10 participants completing assembly tasks, ProcAgent receives positive ratings for comprehensibility, actionability, and privacy comfort. These results show that adaptive procedural assistance can be achieved entirely on edge hardware without sacrificing usability.

AI.tldr: Edge-based, on-device procedural assistant ProcAgent enabling real-time adaptive guidance for furniture assembly, using a propose-and-verify architecture with perception, a symbolic task graph, on-demand vision-language verification, and an LLM-driven interaction agent; achieves low latency and positive user reception without cloud compute.
AI.motivation: Procedural tasks impose high cognitive and perceptual demands (interpreting instructions, tracking progress, spatial reasoning, error recovery). Existing multimodal assistants rely on cloud inference and continuous perception, raising privacy and latency concerns in domestic settings. There is a need for on-device, privacy-preserving, low-latency guidance.
AI.method: Fully on-device system implemented on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Propose-and-verify architecture combining: (i) low-latency continuous perception, (ii) a symbolic task graph to structure steps, (iii) on-demand vision-language verification to resolve ambiguity, and (iv) an LLM-based interaction agent for user communication. The system proposes progress, triggers expensive vision reasoning only on suspected deviations, supports reactive QA and proactive intervention with human-in-the-loop confirmation. Evaluation along perception accuracy, reasoning, task-level performance, and user experience; reported latencies: text-only queries ~2s, visually grounded queries ~8s; user study with 10 participants.
AI.result: ProcAgent runs entirely on-device, maintaining responsive interaction and achieving fast response times without cloud inference. Users rated comprehensibility, actionability, and privacy comfort positively in a task study.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive procedural assistance can be achieved entirely on edge hardware without sacrificing usability.

title: Diff-ID: Identity Consistent Facial Image Generation and Morphing via Diffusion Models
summary: Generative diffusion models have revolutionized facial image synthesis, yet robust identity preservation in high resolution outputs remains a critical challenge. This issue is especially vital for security systems, biometric authentication, and privacy sensitive applications, where any drift in identity integrity can undermine trust and functionality. We introduce Diff-ID, a diffusion based framework that enforces identity consistency while delivering photorealistic quality. Central to our approach is a custom 210K image dataset synthesized from CelebA-HQ, FFHQ, and LAION-Face and captioned via a fine tuned BLIP model to bolster identity awareness during training. Diff-ID integrates ArcFace and CLIP embeddings through a dual cross attention adapter within a fine tuned Stable Diffusion UNet. To further reinforce identity fidelity, we propose a pseudo discriminator loss based on ArcFace cosine similarity with exponential timestep weighting. Experiments on held out and unseen faces show that Diff-ID does not exceed InstantID in raw ArcFace Face Similarity, but achieves substantially lower FID and the strongest FIQ based identity--realism trade off among the evaluated methods. We also present a unified DDIM based morphing pipeline that enables qualitative facial interpolation without per identity fine tuning. We further argue that identity preservation and photorealism should be evaluated jointly rather than in isolation, as high identity similarity alone does not guarantee realistic outputs. To make this trade off explicit, we report Face Image Quality (FIQ) as a complementary ratio based score that combines identity similarity and perceptual realism while keeping FS and FID as the primary metrics.

AI.tldr: Diff-ID is a diffusion-based, identity-preserving facial synthesis framework that combines ArcFace and CLIP guidance in a fine-tuned Stable Diffusion UNet, trained on a synthetic 210k dataset with BLIP captions, and reinforced by a pseudo discriminator loss. It delivers photorealistic outputs with strong identity realism trade-offs, offers a DDIM-based morphing pipeline, and argues for joint evaluation of identity and realism via a novel Face Image Quality (FIQ) metric alongside FID and other baselines.
AI.motivation: Current diffusion models for high-resolution face synthesis struggle to maintain consistent identity, which is critical for security, biometrics, and privacy-sensitive applications. A robust identity-preserving, photorealistic generator is needed that can stabilize identity across samples and enable reliable downstream use.
AI.method: Diff-ID integrates ArcFace and CLIP embeddings through a dual cross-attention adapter into a fine-tuned Stable Diffusion UNet. It uses a synthetic 210k image dataset ( CelebA-HQ, FFHQ, LAION-Face ) captioned by a fine-tuned BLIP model. A pseudo discriminator loss based on ArcFace cosine similarity with exponential timestep weighting reinforces identity fidelity. The framework also includes a unified DDIM-based morphing pipeline for identity-aware interpolation without per-identity fine-tuning.
AI.result: On held-out and unseen faces, Diff-ID does not surpass InstantID in raw ArcFace Face Similarity but achieves substantially lower FID and the strongest Face Image Quality (FIQ) based identity-realism trade-off among evaluated methods.
AI.conclusion: The study advocates joint evaluation of identity preservation and photorealism; introduces FIQ as a ratio-based metric complementing FS and FID; and provides a morphing capability via DDIM, highlighting the importance of combining identity and realism in high-quality facial synthesis for practical, security-sensitive applications.

title: Multiclass Classification without Labels via Posterior Simplex Geometry
summary: In many classification problems, reliable instance-level labels are unavailable. However, it is often possible to construct weakly enriched unlabeled samples: datasets selected by different cuts, sources, populations, or experimental conditions that change latent class proportions without revealing them. Classification without Labels (CWoLa) shows that, in the binary case ($K=2$), a classifier trained to distinguish two impure mixtures with different class proportions can recover an optimal class discriminator without knowing the mixture proportions. We extend this principle to multiclass learning from several unlabeled mixtures ($K>2$), where the learner observes only mixture identity and neither latent class labels nor class-prior matrices. We prove that, for a multiclass mixture model, the Bayes-optimal mixture classifier $g^\star$ maps data points into a $(K-1)$-simplex embedded in mixture-posterior space. The $K$ vertices of this simplex are induced by the latent classes through the unknown mixing matrix. Leveraging this geometry, we propose prior-free procedures that train a standard classifier to distinguish mixture identities and then extract latent class structure using either post-hoc simplex fitting or a bottleneck architecture. Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Galaxy10 DECaLS show that mixture identity alone can recover latent classes and their fractions in the mixture. By narrowing the gap between weakly supervised and fully supervised performance, we provide a mathematically grounded, scalable tool for multiclass discovery in label-scarce domains.

AI.tldr: Extends Classification Without Labels (CWoLa) to multiclass learning from multiple unlabeled mixtures. Proposes a prior-free, geometry-based approach where the Bayes-optimal mixture classifier outputs lie on a (K-1)-simplex in mixture-posterior space; latent classes are recovered via simplex geometry using either post-hoc fitting or a bottleneck model. Demonstrates effectiveness on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Galaxy10 DECaLS, approaching fully supervised performance in label-scarce settings.
AI.motivation: In many domains, reliable instance-level labels are unavailable, but weakly enriched unlabeled samples with differing class proportions exist. Extending CWoLa from binary (K=2) to multiclass (K>2) enables discovery of latent classes and their priors without explicit mixture proportions or class-prior matrices.
AI.method: Prove that the Bayes-optimal mixture classifier g* maps data to a (K-1)-simplex in mixture-posterior space, with the simplex vertices determined by latent classes through the unknown mixing matrix. Propose prior-free procedures: (1) train a standard classifier to distinguish mixture identities; (2) extract latent class structure via (a) post-hoc simplex fitting or (b) a bottleneck architecture that enforces latent-class-like representations. No need for known class priors.
AI.result: Empirical results on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Galaxy10 DECaLS show that mixture identity alone can recover latent classes and their fractions within mixtures. The approach narrows the gap between weakly supervised and fully supervised performance and demonstrates scalable multiclass discovery in label-scarce domains.
AI.conclusion: Provides a mathematically grounded, scalable framework for multiclass discovery from unlabeled mixtures. By leveraging the (K-1)-simplex geometry of the Bayes-optimal classifier in mixture space, it enables latent-class recovery without priors. Further work could address identifiability conditions, robustness to noise, and unknown K or mixing matrices.

title: Leveraging Semantic Maps for City-Scale Cross-View Localization
comment: Equal contribution by Ethan Fahnestock and Erick Fuentes. 13 pages, 7 figures, and 5 tables
summary: We want robots to localize in previously untraversed environments against commonly available prior data. Rich semantic data available from OpenStreetMap can be useful in this task. However, existing methods either ignore this semantic information, directly matching panoramas and overhead imagery, or dramatically compress the semantic information, working with a small set of fixed classes. To leverage this rich semantic information, two challenges need to be overcome. First, useful semantic information needs to be extracted from the robot's egocentric observations. Second, the observed information must be quickly associated with the large prior semantic map (e.g., up to 628 km^2). We show that VLMs are effective at both extracting relevant landmarks from panoramas, and identifying feasible correspondences between these landmarks and prior overhead landmarks. However, using VLMs to propose all correspondences scales poorly as the number of mapped landmarks increases. Instead, we propose distilling a lightweight matcher from a VLM which computes correspondences for all entities in a map. We use this output to form an observation likelihood which is fused over time with a Bayes filter to create a time series of pose estimates. To support further investigation into generalizable cross-view methods that leverage semantic information, we release a dataset of extracted semantics and evaluation trajectories spanning eleven environments, including panoramas we collected in a snowstorm and at night in Boston. We demonstrate our method, trained on a single city's fair-weather data, generalizes across location, lighting, weather, and other challenges. Code and datasets are available at https://efahnestock.github.io/loci/.

AI.tldr: A cross-view localization framework that uses a distilled, lightweight matcher derived from a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to relate egocentric panoramic observations to a large OpenStreetMap-based semantic map, with Bayes-filtered pose estimation and a released dataset across diverse conditions.
AI.motivation: Leverage rich semantic data from OpenStreetMap for localization in previously untraversed environments, addressing the gap where semantic information is either ignored or compressed by existing methods; overcome the scalability challenge of matching many map landmarks.
AI.method: Extract landmarks from egocentric panoramas with a VLM; address scalability by distilling a lightweight matcher that can compute correspondences for all map entities; form an observation likelihood from these correspondences; fuse over time with a Bayes filter to produce a pose time series; release a multi-environment dataset.
AI.result: The method demonstrates generalization across location, lighting, weather, and other challenges; trained on data from one city but effective elsewhere; provides code and datasets for further research.
AI.conclusion: A scalable, generalizable cross-view localization approach that leverages semantic information through a distilled VLM-based matcher, enabling robust pose estimation in large semantic maps and contributing resources for the community.

title: RoCo-ACE: Rollout-Conditioned Online Distillation for Retention-Aware Knowledge Injection
summary: Knowledge injection updates pretrained MLLMs with new factual or domain-specific knowledge, but fitting full authoritative answers can cause drift in non-updated behavior. Online distillation mitigates this drift by training on model-generated rollouts, yet uniform reference-conditioned distillation provides coarse supervision: it can under-emphasize reference-supported rollout tokens and supervise omitted facts only indirectly. We introduce RoCo-ACE, a rollout-conditioned online distillation objective for knowledge injection. RoCo uses same-rollout reference-free/reference-conditioned likelihood contrast to reallocate additional distillation weight to reference-supported rollout tokens, while ACE adds sparse reference-side anchored correction for authoritative anchors omitted from the rollout without full-answer imitation. Across three knowledge-injection settings, six retention benchmarks, multiple baselines, and multiple base models, RoCo-ACE achieves the best injected-knowledge accuracy among compared methods while keeping evaluated retention close to the base model.

AI.tldr: A rollout-conditioned online distillation framework (RoCo-ACE) for injecting knowledge into pretrained multilingual LLMs that reallocates distillation emphasis to reference-supported rollout tokens and adds anchored corrections to omissions, achieving higher injected knowledge accuracy while preserving base-model retention.
AI.motivation: Online distillation helps mitigate drift from knowledge updates, but uniform reference-conditioned supervision can under-emphasize supported facts and miss authoritative anchors. There is a need for a supervision scheme that emphasizes ref-supported rollout tokens while correcting omitted anchors without full-answer imitation.
AI.method: Introduce RoCo-ACE: RoCo uses same-rollout likelihood contrasts (reference-free and reference-conditioned) to reweight distillation toward reference-supported rollout tokens; ACE adds sparse reference-side anchored correction to incorporate authoritative anchors omitted in rollout. Combined as RoCo-ACE, evaluated across three settings, six benchmarks, multiple models/baselines.
AI.result: RoCo-ACE achieves the best injected-knowledge accuracy among compared methods and retains retention close to the base model across tasks and settings.
AI.conclusion: RoCo-ACE provides an effective framework for knowledge injection that balances insertion of new facts with retention of non-updated behavior in multilingual LLMs, by combining rollout-conditioned distillation emphasis with anchored corrections.

title: MorphUNet: Alpha-Controlled Biometric Transport for Diffusion-Based Face Morphing Attacks
comment: 37 pages, 23 figures, 8 tables. Includes supplementary material (additional robustness analysis, CFD stress tests, and conditioning ablations) appended after the references
summary: Face morphing attacks create synthetic images verifiable against multiple identities, threatening border control and identity verification systems. We introduce MorphUNet, a diffusion morphing framework formulating two-parent generation as alpha-controlled biometric transport: each parent is decomposed into CLIP appearance and ArcFace identity evidence, aligned into a CLIP-compatible token space, with the two contributors preserved as separate identity-aware token banks. To our knowledge, MorphUNet is the first diffusion-based morphing framework using trainable parent-separated dual cross-attention inside the denoising U-Net: a Biometric Transport Layer carrying parent-specific identity evidence through denoising, attending to each parent separately before combining residuals via the morphing parameter alpha. DDIM-inverted latent interpolation gives a coherent denoising start, while weaker-parent-guided selection favours morphs maximising the lower parent-similarity score, reducing collapse toward one contributor. We evaluate MorphUNet against three state-of-the-art baselines (StableMorph, MIPGAN-II, and MorDIFF) on FEI and FRLL using six recognition systems, and propose CFD-based unseen-identity stress testing across gender and ethnicity pairing, demographic shifts, and parent-similarity extremes. MorphUNet achieves the best Morphing Attack Potential (MAP) when at least three of six systems are fooled by one morph, reaching 0.919 on FEI and 0.886 on FRLL, and obtains the best FID on both datasets (35.19 FEI, 44.86 FRLL). It also gives the highest APCER at 5% BPCER in the same-dataset setting, and remains highly difficult to detect under cross-dataset transfer, with APCER 0.996 on FEI and 0.946 on FRLL. The full evaluation analyses MAP, MAD, per-system vulnerability, identity balance, image quality, top/bottom-similarity stress tests, and CFD unseen-identity robustness.

AI.tldr: MorphUNet is a diffusion-based two-parent face-morphing framework that uses alpha-controlled biometric transport with parent-separated dual cross-attention in a denoising U-Net, achieving leading Morphing Attack Potential (MAP) and image quality while remaining hard to detect across datasets.
AI.motivation: To enable high-fidelity, controllable morphs that threaten identity verification systems and to provide comprehensive evaluation, including unseen-identity stress testing across demographics.
AI.method: Diffusion-based architecture where each parent is decomposed into CLIP appearance and ArcFace identity evidence, aligned in a CLIP-compatible token space with separate identity-aware token banks. A Biometric Transport Layer carries parent-specific evidence through denoising, attending to each parent via dual cross-attention, combined by a morphing parameter alpha. DDIM-inverted latent interpolation initializes denoising; weaker-parent-guided selection biases toward morphs with higher low-parent similarity. Evaluated against StableMorph, MIPGAN-II, MorDIFF on FEI/FRLL using six recognition systems and CFD-based unseen-identity stress testing across gender, ethnicity, and similarity extremes.
AI.result: MorphUNet achieves the best MAP when at least three of six systems are fooled (MAP up to 0.919 on FEI and 0.886 on FRLL). It yields the best FID on both datasets (35.19 FEI, 44.86 FRLL) and the highest APCER at 5% BPCER in the same-dataset setting. It remains highly challenging to detect under cross-dataset transfer (APCER 0.996 FEI, 0.946 FRLL). The full evaluation covers MAP, MAD, per-system vulnerability, identity balance, image quality, top/bottom-similarity stress tests, and CFD unseen-identity robustness.
AI.conclusion: MorphUNet constitutes a novel diffusion-based morphing framework with trainable, parent-separated dual cross-attention and a Biometric Transport Layer, enabling controllable, high-quality morphs with strong performance across multiple metrics, while revealing persistent detection challenges and robustness under unseen identities.

title: Stable FP4 Training via Transposition-Invariant Block Quantization
summary: Reducing training precision is a key lever for improving the e ciency of large language model (LLM) training, but pushing beyond FP8 to 4-bit oating point (FP4) remains challenging due to instability during optimization. We identify a fundamental source of this instability in existing microscaling approaches: scale inconsistency induced by tensor transposition. In conventional 1D block quantization, forward and backward passes assign di erent scaling factors to the same values after transposition, leading to biased and unstable gradient updates. To address this issue, we propose a low-precision training framework based on 2D block FP4 quantization, which enforces transposition-invariant scaling and preserves consistency between forward and backward computations. We further combine this with truncation-free scaling and stochastic rounding to control quantization error and maintain unbiased gradients. To handle the sensitivity of attention mechanisms, we adopt MXFP8 quantization for query and key projections, yielding a practical mixed-precision design. We evaluate our method on dense LLMs up to 7B parameters and a 30B Mixture-of-Experts model, trained on up to 100B tokens. Across all settings, our approach achieves stable end-to-end FP4 training and closely matches BF16 performance, with less than 1.3% degradation in perplexity and downstream accuracy. These results demonstrate that enforcing forwardbackward scaling consistency is su cient to enable practical FP4 training at scale, providing a simple and e ective pathway toward more e cient LLM training.

AI.tldr: 2D block FP4 quantization with transposition-invariant scaling enables stable end-to-end FP4 training for large language models, closely matching BF16 performance with minimal accuracy loss.
AI.motivation: FP4 offers substantial training efficiency gains, but instability arises from scale inconsistency during transposition in 1D block quantization. A transposition‑invariant, stable scaling scheme is needed for practical FP4 training at scale.
AI.method: Introduce 2D block FP4 quantization that enforces transposition-invariant scaling; apply truncation-free scaling and stochastic rounding to control quantization error; adopt MXFP8 quantization for query/key projections to handle attention sensitivity; compile a mixed‑precision design; evaluate on dense LLMs up to 7B and a 30B Mixture-of-Experts model, trained on up to 100B tokens.
AI.result: Stable end-to-end FP4 training achieved across tested models; performance closely matches BF16 with less than 1.3% degradation in perplexity and downstream accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Enforcing forward-backward scaling consistency suffices to enable practical FP4 training at scale, offering a simple and effective path to more efficient LLM training.

title: SONG: A Photorealistic 3D Gaussian Simulation Platform for Benchmarking Social Navigation
summary: Social navigation has progressed from simplified 2D environments toward a more general vision-based setting, in which a robot needs to achieve socially compliant behavior purely from onboard visual observations. Yet supporting simulation platforms have not kept pace: existing options either lack visual observations, lack moving human avatars, or fall short of real-world fidelity in appearance and pedestrian behavior, offering limited support for advancing vision-based social navigation. We introduce SONG, a SOcial Navigation platform powered by 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS). It leverages 3DGS for both scene and avatar representations, drives pedestrians using semantically grounded trajectories generated by a large language model, and synthesizes their full-body motion with a trajectory-conditioned generator to produce continuous, natural movement. On top of the platform, we curate SONG-Bench, a set of evaluation episodes stratified by difficulty, and propose a multi-dimensional metric suite covering effectiveness, safety, and social compliance. A systematic evaluation of representative navigation baselines reveals three findings: (a) vision-based social navigation is far from solved; (b) a critical safety deficit precedes social etiquette; (c) real-world data matters more than model scale. Crucially, we demonstrate that fine-tuning on our curated data effectively improves the success rate in real-world environments. We hope our platform provides a faithful and rigorous testbed for the next generation of vision-based social navigation research.

AI.tldr: Proposes SONG, a vision-based social navigation platform using 3D Gaussian splatting for scene/avatars, LLM-driven semantically grounded pedestrian trajectories, and a trajectory-conditioned full-body motion generator; introduces SONG-Bench and a multi-metric evaluation; finds vision-based social navigation is not solved, safety gaps precede etiquette, real-world data is more impactful than model scale; fine-tuning on curated data improves real-world success.
AI.motivation: Address the lack of capable, realistic vision-based social navigation simulators that provide onboard visual observations and moving human avatars, enabling robust evaluation and development.
AI.method: Employ 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) for scene and avatar representations; generate semantically grounded pedestrian trajectories using a large language model; synthesize full-body motion with a trajectory-conditioned generator; construct SONG-Bench as a tiered evaluation suite; evaluate with a multi-dimensional metric set (effectiveness, safety, social compliance).
AI.result: Systematic evaluation reveals that (a) vision-based social navigation remains challenging; (b) safety gaps precede social etiquette issues; (c) real-world data matters more than model scale; fine-tuning on curated SONG data improves success rates in real environments.
AI.conclusion: SONG provides a faithful, rigorous testbed to advance vision-based social navigation research, highlighting the importance of real-world data and the need for integrated perception-action pipelines.

title: RSMeM: Knowledge-Enhanced Memory Evolution for Remote Sensing Agents with Systematic Evaluation
comment: Accepted to ACL 2026 Main. Code: https://github.com/AI9Stars/RSMeM
summary: Geoscience research requires complex analysis and domain expertise, with remote sensing (RS) observations as a key foundation. However, existing RS agents built on general-purpose LLMs remain largely domain-agnostic, resulting in brittle and error-prone workflows. Moreover, these failures are seldom consolidated into a reusable experience for subsequent analyses. To address this issue, we introduce RSMeM, a knowledge-enhanced memory evolution mechanism that bootstraps RS agents with pre-distilled domain knowledge and iteratively integrates online experience for robust multi-step tool execution. RSMeM is composed of two components: (i) Hierarchical Knowledge Grounding, which performs taxonomy-aware retrieval over a hierarchical domain corpus to guide planning and tool selection; and (ii) Failure-Aware Experience Refinement, which distills failure-annotated tool-use traces into reusable constraints for next-round tool execution. By iteratively employing these two processes, RS agents can evolve to absorb task-level domain knowledge and effectively translate it into instance-level execution experience. Extensive experiments on EarthBench demonstrate that RSMeM consistently improves tool-use performance and end-to-end answer across a diverse set of LLM backbones. Notably, RSMeM achieves a 6% accuracy improvement on DeepSeek-V3.2 with less than 1% additional experience tokens, demonstrating the strong knowledge density of our distilled experience. Our code is available at https://github.com/AI9Stars/RSMeM

AI.tldr: RSMeM is a knowledge-enhanced memory mechanism for remote-sensing agents that combines hierarchical knowledge grounding with failure-aware experience refinement to enable robust, multi-step tool use and knowledge evolution, yielding improved performance with minimal extra data.
AI.motivation: Domain-agnostic, brittle RS agents lack task-level knowledge and reusable execution experience; integrating domain knowledge and online experience can improve robustness and accuracy.
AI.method: Two components: (i) Hierarchical Knowledge Grounding — taxonomy-aware retrieval over a hierarchical domain corpus to guide planning and tool selection; (ii) Failure-Aware Experience Refinement — distills failure-annotated tool-use traces into reusable constraints for subsequent rounds. The method iterates these steps to evolve task-level knowledge into instance-level execution.
AI.result: On EarthBench, RSMeM improves tool-use performance and end-to-end answers across diverse LLM backbones; achieves about 6% accuracy gain on DeepSeek-V3.2 with <1% additional experience tokens, indicating strong knowledge density of distilled experience. Code is available at the referenced GitHub repository.
AI.conclusion: RSMeM demonstrates effective knowledge-grounded and experience-driven adaptation for RS agents, enabling robust multi-step tool execution and knowledge evolution with minimal data, and is readily integrable with existing LLM backbones.

title: IMPRINT: Image-Conditioned Query Enrichment for Long-Tail Object Goal Navigation
comment: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS). Project page: https://github.com/JelinR/IMPRINT
summary: Embodied AI increasingly relies on queryable semantic maps built from pre-trained vision-language models to enable zero-shot Object Goal Navigation (ObjectNav). However, existing approaches typically depend on text-only queries, which become less reliable as semantic specificity increases toward fine-grained object categories. We introduce IMPRINT, a zero-shot plug-and-play framework that enriches textual object queries with web-sourced images to improve grounding in queryable maps. Retrieved images are encoded using a vision-language model, matched against the semantic map to produce similarity maps, and aggregated to yield context-aware localization. Notably, this requires no training or modification of the underlying navigation policy. To explicitly evaluate long-tail behavior, we present HSSD-rare, a new ObjectNav benchmark built on Habitat Synthetic Scenes and featuring semantically specific subcategories. Across both OVON and HSSD-rare, image-conditioned queries consistently improve object grounding and yield end-to-end navigation gains. Further analysis reveals that translating localization gains to navigation performance depends critically on downstream detection quality, highlighting a key systems bottleneck in long-tail embodied navigation.

AI.tldr: IMPRINT enriches text queries with web-sourced images to improve grounding in semantic maps for zero-shot ObjectNav, without training, and shows gains on OVON and a new long-tail benchmark HSSD-rare; bottleneck lies in downstream detection.
AI.motivation: Text-only object queries struggle with fine-grained categories; enriching queries with visual context can improve grounding in queryable maps and enable better zero-shot ObjectNav without retraining.
AI.method: Retrieve web images for object queries; encode with a vision-language model to produce image embeddings; compare against semantic map to generate similarity maps; aggregate into context-aware localization; plug-and-play, requiring no changes to the navigation policy or training.
AI.result: Image-conditioned queries yield improved object grounding and end-to-end navigation gains on OVON and HSSD-rare; however, the extent of navigation improvement depends on downstream detection quality.
AI.conclusion: IMPRINT provides a training-free boost to grounding in semantic maps for long-tail ObjectNav, but a key bottleneck remains downstream detection performance that limits translation of localization gains into navigation success.

title: Generative Distributionally Robust Optimization
summary: Generative models are increasingly adopted in distributionally robust optimization (DRO), but existing approaches trade off model compatibility and adversarial structure: methods that accept arbitrary samplers do not restrict worst-case laws to a generator family, while generator-parameterized adversaries rely on model-specific access such as likelihoods, scores, or training data. We propose Generative Distributionally Robust Optimization (GDRO), a principled framework that accepts any sampleable conditional generator as the nominal model and restricts worst-case laws to a chosen conditional generator family. The key is the sampler-Sinkhorn pairing: samplers represent the conditional laws exactly, while Sinkhorn divergence compares their induced distributions without likelihood access and can be estimated from samples alone. The resulting population problem admits a direct finite-sample approximation and differentiable primal-dual implementation at the active decision context. For Lipschitz losses, the population Sinkhorn radius bounds downstream degradation. Across explicit and implicit generators, our method reduces rare-context inventory regret by 60% and SocialGAN navigation collisions by 50% relative to nominal decisions.

AI.tldr: GDRO leverages a sampler-Sinkhorn pairing to allow any conditional generator as the nominal model while constraining adversaries to a chosen generator family, enabling sample-based, differentiable optimization with provable bounds and practical performance gains.
AI.motivation: Fix the trade-off in DRO between model compatibility and adversarial structure by enabling a flexible nominal generator and a restricted, generator-based worst-case law.
AI.method: Introduce sampler-Sinkhorn pairing: samplers represent conditional laws exactly; Sinkhorn divergence measures distance between induced distributions from samples without requiring likelihood access. Formulate a population problem with a finite-sample approximation and a differentiable primal-dual algorithm for the active decision context.
AI.result: For Lipschitz losses, the population Sinkhorn radius bounds downstream degradation. Empirically, across explicit and implicit generators, GDRO reduces rare-context inventory regret by 60% and SocialGAN navigation collisions by 50% relative to nominal decisions.
AI.conclusion: GDRO provides a principled, scalable framework to combine arbitrary generators with a controlled worst-case distributional shift, offering tractable estimation from samples and tangible gains in heterogeneous tasks.

title: Belief-Aware Influence and Trust (BAIT): Shaping Human Belief During Repeated Human-Robot Interaction
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letter (RA-L)
summary: Repeated human-robot interaction (HRI) requires proactively accounting for humans who continually adapt to evolving beliefs about the robot. Prior frameworks often treat encounters as isolated events, suffering cumulative task performance decay as human perception drifts, or maintain long-term influence through erratic, unpredictable behavior that erodes perceived human trust and relies on computationally unscalable formulations. To address these gaps, we introduce the Belief- Aware Influence and Trust (BAIT) controller. BAIT integrates a hierarchical particle filter, which infers both fast human strategic shifts and slow perceptual belief updates, with a belief-aware Model Predictive Path Integral planner. BAIT explicitly optimizes the trade-off between long-horizon influence and human trust, while enforcing immediate task performance as a strict constraint. Across simulations, a human-subject study, and a real-world GEM vehicle deployments in repeated lane-merging scenarios, BAIT achieves task performance comparable to baselines that optimize long-term influence through unpredictability while yielding significantly higher user trust. The video demonstrating our experiments is available at https://youtu.be/GsPfHRujzVs.

AI.tldr: BAIT integrates a hierarchical particle filter with a belief-aware MPPI planner to manage evolving human beliefs in repeated HRI, balancing long-horizon influence and trust while enforcing immediate task performance, yielding higher trust with comparable performance across simulations, a user study, and real-world lane-merging deployments.
AI.motivation: Existing frameworks treat HRI encounters as isolated events and fail to account for co-evolving human beliefs, leading to performance decay or reliance on unpredictable behavior that erodes trust; there is a need for belief-aware control that is scalable and maintains task constraints.
AI.method: A hierarchical particle filter infers both fast human strategic shifts and slow perceptual belief updates. A belief-aware Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) planner optimizes the trade-off between long-horizon influence and human trust, while enforcing immediate task performance as a hard constraint. Validation spans simulations, a human-subject study, and real-world GEM vehicle deployments in repeated lane-merging scenarios.
AI.result: BAIT achieves task performance comparable to baselines that pursue long-term influence via unpredictability but yields significantly higher user trust in all evaluated settings.
AI.conclusion: Belief-aware control via BAIT successfully addresses evolving human beliefs in repeated HRI, balancing influence and trust without sacrificing immediate task performance, and demonstrates effectiveness in both simulated and real-world driving tasks.

title: Right-sizing Recommendations (RSR): Cloud Workload Conformal Prediction for Virtual Machines in Data Center Operations
comment: 10 pages, 10 figures. Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 2025 IEEE/WIC International Conference on Web Intelligence and Intelligent Agent Technology (WI-IAT 2025). Author Accepted Manuscript
summary:
Managing cloud infrastructure efficiently, especially in environments of large cloud providers or hyperscalers, requires optimizing the use of physical resources to minimize costs and maximize performance. Selecting the right virtual machine (VM) sizes is crucial to achieving cost efficiency in these dynamic environments. However, traditional VM allocation and scheduling approaches often fail to account for the fluctuating and unpredictable nature of VM utilization, leading to inefficiencies such as over- or under-provisioning of resources. High-quality interval prediction helps accurately capture uncertainty in cloud resource demand and supports cloud operators in efficient instance provisioning.
  As an effective and reliable framework for constructing prediction intervals (PIs), conformal prediction (CP) is used for mid- and long-term forecasting tasks in cloud computing environments. This study proposes a new data-driven PI construction approach using bootstrapping conformal prediction for modern, dynamic, data-driven Right-sizing Recommendations (RSR) to enhance provisioning for diverse application workloads on hyperscalers. By learning workload utilization patterns, identifying correlations across multiple time series, and predicting medium- to long-term utilization trends, this research seeks to improve the efficiency of cloud and data center operations through an AI/ML-based provisioning pipeline.
  Our study demonstrates that AI-driven models, powered by machine learning regression techniques and evaluated using backtesting, achieve promising forecasting results for cloud resource utilization. Additionally, we rank the selected models to identify top-performing approaches for long-life VM candidates. The proposed framework enhances right-sizing recommendations and supports more cost-effective resource allocation in dynamic cloud environments.

AI.tldr: Bootstrapped conformal prediction for data-driven right-sizing of VMs in hyperscale clouds, using ML regression and backtesting to produce prediction intervals for medium- to long-term resource utilization and guide cost-efficient provisioning.
AI.motivation: In hyperscalers, efficient resource use and accurate provisioning are critical amid fluctuating demand; conventional VM allocation under-provisions or over-provisions due to uncertain workloads; high-quality PIs are needed to support robust right-sizing decisions.
AI.method: Construct prediction intervals via bootstrapping conformal prediction; learn workload patterns and cross-series correlations; apply ML regression models; backtest the forecasting pipeline; rank models to identify top performers for long-life VM candidates; integrate into an AI-driven provisioning pipeline.
AI.result: Backtesting-based evaluation shows promising accuracy of AI-driven ML models for cloud resource utilization; model ranking isolates top approaches for long-life VM candidates; framework improves right-sizing and cost-efficiency in dynamic cloud environments.
AI.conclusion: A data-driven CP-based PI construction framework augmented with bootstrapping enables more reliable long-horizon provisioning decisions, yielding improved resource utilization and reduced over-/under-provisioning in hyperscale clouds.

title: OPERA: Offline Policy-guided Expert Routing and Adaptation for Universal Biomedical Image Analysis
summary: Biomedical image analysis spans diverse modalities and tasks, yet real-world deployment is hindered by severe distribution shifts across scanners, protocols, and patient populations. High-performing models consequently require repeated domain-specific fine-tuning, which is a costly cycle that becomes impractical when labels are scarce or privacy constraints limit data sharing. We propose OPERA (Offline Policy-guided Expert Routing and Adaptation), a multi-agent ensemble framework that addresses this deployment bottleneck by treating expert weight assignment as an offline policy learning problem: a routing policy is learned from a small validation set without gradient updates to any expert agent, then deployed with test-time adaptation to handle distribution shift. OPERA coordinates heterogeneous specialist agents through complementary mechanisms. The expert profiling module learns selection policies offline, enabling informed allocation of expertise. Each agent undergoes confidence calibration through temperature adjustment, ensuring more reliable probabilistic outputs. OPERA also incorporates distribution aware adaptation, where class weights are dynamically adjusted at the batch level using statistics derived from unlabeled test data. Instance level routing assigns each sample to the most suitable expert by leveraging inter model agreement and predictive entropy. We evaluate OPERA on 9 datasets covering fundus photography, chest X-ray, CT, MRI, and multimodal diagnostic benchmarks, comparing against 30+ baselines across classification, segmentation, and multimodal settings. OPERA consistently improves performance and calibration quality, demonstrating that offline policy-guided expert agents coordination is a practical path to deployable biomedical AI without retraining. Code is on \href{https://github.com/HUANGLIZI/OPERA}{GitHub}.

AI.tldr: OPERA is an offline policy-guided, multi-agent ensemble for robust biomedical image analysis under distribution shifts. It learns a routing policy offline from a small validation set to coordinate diverse expert models without retraining, while applying test-time adaptation (class-weight adjustments and instance-level routing) and temperature calibration to improve calibration and performance. Evaluated on 9 datasets across multiple modalities, it consistently outperforms 30+ baselines and is released with code.
AI.motivation: Biomedical Image Analysis suffers from severe distribution shifts across scanners, protocols, and populations, forcing costly domain-specific fine-tuning and retraining—impractical when labels are scarce or data sharing is restricted. An offline, deployable routing framework can leverage existing experts to adapt without retraining.
AI.method: OPERA treats expert weight assignment as offline policy learning. It comprises: (1) expert profiling to learn offline selection policies without changing expert weights; (2) confidence calibration via temperature scaling for reliable outputs; (3) distribution-aware adaptation with batch-level class-weight adjustments inferred from unlabeled test data; (4) instance-level routing using inter-model agreement and predictive entropy to assign each sample to the most suitable expert. Routing policy is learned on a small validation set and deployed with test-time adaptation; no gradient updates to any expert. Evaluation spans nine datasets (fundus, chest X-ray, CT, MRI, multimodal) against 30+ baselines across classification, segmentation, and multimodal tasks; code available on GitHub.
AI.result: OPERA consistently delivers improved performance and improved calibration quality compared to baselines across diverse tasks and modalities, demonstrating that offline policy-guided coordination of specialist agents is a practical path toward deployable biomedical AI without retraining.
