summary: Stereo depth estimation for driving, robotics and augmented reality must run at high resolution under tight latency budgets, yet in transformer-based matchers the global self-attention that aggregates scene context grows quadratically with the number of pixels and comes to dominate runtime. We show that the joint self-attention stage of a stereo transformer, whose role is to spread context across both views, can be replaced by a data-independent Walsh-Hadamard token mixer that mixes tokens globally in the transform domain at log-linear cost, while the data-dependent cross-attention that performs left-right correspondence is retained. On synthetic driving data the mixer matches the attention baseline in end-point error while reducing model compute by a factor of 2.46 and single-image inference latency by a factor of 2.65. A complexity analysis shows the benefit is governed by the ratio of sequence length to channel width, which explains why high-resolution stereo matching is a particularly favorable setting and why classification transformers are not; we confirm this token-to-channel scaling on non-stereo long-sequence benchmarks. Furthermore, we introduce a hybrid log-disparity loss function designed to up-weight small-disparity pixels corresponding to long-range objects. This approach reduces the error on distant objects without incurring any additional computational overhead.

AI.tldr: Replacing joint self-attention in stereo transformers with a Walsh-Hadamard token mixer yields log-linear scaling, maintaining accuracy while reducing compute and latency; supplemented by a hybrid log-disparity loss to better handle distant objects.
AI.motivation: High-resolution stereo depth estimation under tight latency budgets; standard transformer self-attention scales quadratically with pixels, hindering real-time use.
AI.method: Substitute the data-independent Walsh-Hadamard mixer for the joint self-attention stage; keep data-dependent cross-attention for left-right correspondence; analyze complexity; introduce hybrid log-disparity loss.
AI.result: On synthetic driving data, achieves similar end-point error to attention baseline while reducing compute by ~2.46x and latency by ~2.65x; complexity analysis links benefit to sequence length to channel width; validates scaling on non-stereo long sequences; log-disparity loss reduces distant-object errors without extra compute.
AI.conclusion: Joint self-attention can be replaced by a log-linear mixer in stereo transformers without sacrificing accuracy; complexity gains are explained by geometry; the approach extends with a loss that improves distant object handling.

title: Physics-Informed CNN-LSTM for Street-Scale Urban Flood Prediction: Reconciling Aggregate Accuracy and Street-Level Plausibility
summary: Deep learning surrogate models trained with mean-squared-error loss produce statistically accurate but physically unconstrained flood predictions: water may flow uphill, appear spontaneously, or smooth over street-level corridors. We develop a physics-informed training framework for CNN-LSTM models that predict urban flood depths at 15 min intervals over a 128x128 spatial grid. Three differentiable penalty terms are embedded into the loss: (i) a gravity loss penalizing depth increases against the water-surface-elevation gradient, (ii) a continuity loss enforcing local mass conservation with rainfall-adaptive thresholds, and (iii) a topography-aware false-alarm penalty modulated by the topographic wetness index (TWI). We evaluate on the Norfolk, Virginia flood dataset spanning two storm events (August 2017 and September 2022, 300 samples), with all variants trained on identical splits and robustness assessed over repeated random splits and leave-one-storm-out tests. A road-proximal evaluation restricted to a TWI-derived street mask quantifies street-level skill. The physics-constrained model achieves near-zero gravity violations (order 1e-6) and the highest street-channel recall (0.77 +/- 0.09 vs 0.44 +/- 0.10 for the unconstrained baseline), the capability most relevant to traffic routing, and its advantage more than doubles on a held-out storm; a uniform false-alarm variant attains 16% lower mean absolute error but suppresses street recall to 0.25. The TWI-modulated penalty reconciles this trade-off: it improves on the uniform variant on every metric, recovering 60% higher street recall at the lowest MAE among constrained variants and the best street-level F1. These results expose a fundamental tension between aggregate pixel-level error and application-specific physical plausibility, and show that terrain-aware loss modulation offers a principled resolution.

AI.tldr: Physics-informed loss improves physical plausibility and street-level accuracy in urban flood depth forecasting with CNN-LSTM; a terrain-aware, TWI-modulated penalty yields the best trade-off between accuracy and plausibility.
AI.motivation: Standard mean-squared-error training yields statistically accurate but physically unconstrained flood predictions (e.g., uphill flow). Embedding physics-based penalties aims to enforce gravity consistency, local mass conservation, and reduce false alarms in a terrain-aware manner to improve practical utility for routing and decision-making.
AI.method: CNN-LSTM model forecasts 15-minute flood depths on a 128×128 grid. Loss includes three differentiable penalties: (i) gravity loss penalizing depth increases against the water-surface-elevation gradient, (ii) continuity loss enforcing local mass conservation with rainfall-adaptive thresholds, and (iii) topography-aware false-alarm penalty modulated by the topographic wetness index (TWI). Trained and evaluated on the Norfolk, VA flood dataset across two storm events (Aug 2017, Sep 2022; 300 samples). Experiments use identical splits, repeated random splits, and leave-one-storm-out tests; road-proximal street-level performance is assessed via a TWI-derived street mask.
AI.result: The physics-constrained model shows near-zero gravity violations (~1e-6) and the highest street-channel recall (0.77±0.09) versus unconstrained baseline (0.44±0.10). Compared to a held-out storm, this advantage doubles. A uniform false-alarm variant reduces MAE by ~16% but lowers street recall to ~0.25. The TWI-modulated penalty improves on the uniform variant across metrics, achieving ~60% higher street recall at the lowest MAE among constrained variants and the best street-level F1. The study highlights a tension between pixel-level MAE and application-specific physical plausibility, withterrain-aware loss modulation offering a principled resolution.
AI.conclusion: Terrain-aware, physics-informed loss terms can markedly improve physical plausibility and street-level utility in data-driven flood forecasting without sacrificing overall accuracy; the approach provides a balanced framework for integrating domain physics (gravity, mass conservation, terrain) into predictive models, and the TWI modulation effectively negotiates the trade-off between false alarms and street-level performance.

title: Tri-Manual Visuomotor Imitation Learning of Robot Policies
comment: 9 pages, 9 figures. Equal contribution by James Zhao and Mingyuan Ba
summary: Bimanual teleoperation provides an effective way to collect robot demonstrations, but it assumes that the operator and robot have matching numbers of simultaneous control channels. This assumption breaks for tri-manual systems: the robot can coordinate three arms concurrently, whereas a single operator can continuously control only two. Pairwise mode switching may therefore record otherwise independent motions sequentially, causing behaviour cloning to reproduce delays imposed by the interface rather than required by the task. We present TriManPolicy, a tri-manual imitation learning system that allows one operator to demonstrate behaviours for three arms. Its central component is Dependency-Aware Tri-Arm Scheduling (DATS). The key idea is to preserve the demonstrated arm motions while reconsidering when they occur. DATS retimes demonstrations offline by preserving local sensorimotor segments of fixed duration and repositioning them according to constraints on task order and arm usage that are reviewed by a human. The resulting data train a single synchronous policy for all three arms, while deployment requires neither the dependency graph nor the scheduler. Across six challenging tasks performed in the real world, policies trained on demonstrations retimed by DATS exhibit more efficient coordination while maintaining comparable observed task success. Offline analysis further shows that DATS changes the supervision across arms rather than merely removing idle periods.

AI.tldr: TriManPolicy enables a single operator to demonstrate three robotic arms by offline retiming via Dependency-Aware Tri-Arm Scheduling (DATS), yielding a synchronous, efficient policy without modifying deployment.
AI.motivation: Tri-manual systems break the assumption of matching operator control channels; pairwise switching introduces task-dependent delays that bias learned policies.
AI.method: Introduce DATS to retime demonstrations offline, preserving fixed-duration local segments and reordering them under task-order and arm-usage constraints reviewed by a human; train a single synchronous policy for all three arms; deployment does not require the dependency graph or scheduler.
AI.result: In six real-world tasks, policies trained with DATS show improved coordination efficiency while maintaining comparable success; offline analysis shows DATS alters supervision across arms rather than just removing idle time.
AI.conclusion: DATS enables efficient tri-arm imitation learning from a single demonstration stream, facilitating tri-manual manipulation with preserved task semantics and practical deployment benefits.

title: SpecPrefetch: Parameter-Efficient Expert Prefetching for Sparse MoE Foundation Models
summary: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models expand foundation model capacity through conditional expert activation, but their full expert pools remain difficult to deploy under limited accelerator memory. Although expert offloading alleviates memory pressure by moving inactive experts to host memory or storage, it introduces a routing-dependent transfer bottleneck: required experts are known only after native top-\(K\) routing, which serializes routing, expert loading, and expert execution during inference. To address this bottleneck, we propose SpecPrefetch, a parameter-efficient prefetching framework for offloaded MoE inference. SpecPrefetch uses a shared lightweight adapter to predict next-layer expert candidates only for asynchronous transfer, while the frozen native router still determines the final executed experts. By separating transfer prediction from execution routing, SpecPrefetch reduces exposed expert-loading latency without changing pretrained routing semantics, so prediction errors affect transfer efficiency rather than model outputs. In addition, a window-aware scheduler prioritizes feasible transfers under cache and bandwidth constraints. Across Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B and DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny, SpecPrefetch achieves the best average expert recall in 9 out of 10 model-benchmark settings with substantially fewer trainable parameters than learned predictor baselines. On a Snapdragon 8 Elite device, SpecPrefetch further improves decoding throughput by up to \(20\%\) over a compute-optimized offloading runtime, demonstrating practical benefits for storage-constrained MoE deployment. The code and model weights are available at https://github.com/wei390/SpecPrefetch.

AI.tldr: SpecPrefetch is a parameter-efficient prefetching framework for offloaded MoE inference that decouples transfer prediction from routing to reduce expert-loading latency without altering routing semantics.
AI.motivation: Sparse MoE models use large expert pools that exceed accelerator memory; offloading inactive experts helps, but requires routing-dependent loading that serializes routing, loading, and execution, creating a bottleneck.
AI.method: A shared lightweight adapter predicts next-layer expert candidates for asynchronous prefetching of offloaded experts. The native router remains responsible for final executed experts. A window-aware scheduler prioritizes feasible transfers under cache and bandwidth constraints, enabling asynchronous transfers without changing routing semantics.
AI.result: Across Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B and DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny, SpecPrefetch achieves the best average expert recall in 9 of 10 settings, with substantially fewer trainable parameters than learned predictor baselines. On a Snapdragon 8 Elite device, decoding throughput improves up to 20% over a compute-optimized offloading runtime.
AI.conclusion: SpecPrefetch demonstrates that separating transfer prediction from routing can reduce exposure latency and improve practicality for storage-constrained MoE deployment, with minimal risk to model outputs and tangible hardware throughput gains.

title: CD-RMOT-Bench: Benchmarking the Cross-Domain Referring Multi-Object Tracking
summary: Referring multi-object tracking (RMOT) extends tracking from category-driven perception to language-guided understanding by grounding object trajectories in natural-language expressions. Despite recent progress, existing RMOT studies are largely conducted under in-domain settings, leaving the robustness of language-conditioned tracking under inevitable visual domain shifts unexplored. In this paper, we study Cross-Domain Referring Multi-Object Tracking (CD-RMOT), a new and challenging problem that evaluates whether an RMOT model trained on a labeled source domain can reliably follow natural-language expressions in an unlabeled target domain with different visual conditions. To support systematic study, we construct CD-RMOT-Bench, a unified benchmark that combines real clear-domain referring tracking data, aligned digital-twin variants, and real adverse-domain videos. CD-RMOT-Bench enables both controlled weather/viewpoint shift analysis and realistic synthetic-real transfer evaluation under a shared RMOT protocol. Further, we provide a Query-Centric Adaptation (QCA) framework, designed to stabilize the query space that bridges visual trajectories and referring expressions. Extensive experiments reveal that domain shifts severely degrade RMOT performance, where the failure is not merely caused by object detection errors but more critically by unstable expression-conditioned temporal association and target selection. QCA establishes a strong baseline, while CD-RMOT-Bench opens a new direction for robust language-guided tracking across visual domains.

AI.tldr: Introduces Cross-Domain Referring Multi-Object Tracking (CD-RMOT) with a unified benchmark (CD-RMOT-Bench) and a Query-Centric Adaptation (QCA) framework to study and improve robustness of language-guided tracking under visual-domain shifts.
AI.motivation: Existing RMOT works assume in-domain data; domain shifts degrade performance, especially in expression-conditioned temporal association; there is a need for systematic cross-domain evaluation and robust adaptation in language-guided tracking.
AI.method: Develop CD-RMOT-Bench by combining real clear-domain data, aligned digital-twin variants, and real adverse-domain videos; propose QCA to stabilize the query space bridging trajectories and natural-language expressions.
AI.result: Experiments show domain shifts markedly degrade RMOT; the main failure mode is unstable expression-conditioned temporal association and target selection rather than detector errors; QCA provides a strong baseline; CD-RMOT-Bench enables controlled evaluation and cross-domain transfer studies.
AI.conclusion: CD-RMOT-Bench enables robust evaluation of language-guided tracking across domains; QCA offers a practical baseline for cross-domain RMOT; results motivate further research on cross-domain robustness in RMOT.

title: Accurate structural modeling of chemically diverse molecular interfaces with Vilya-2
summary: Structure-prediction networks built on co-evolutionary statistics have transformed protein-based drug discovery, yet their accuracy does not extend to peptide therapeutics--an increasingly important modality defined by non-canonical residues, macrocyclization, and complex topologies. We introduce Vilya-2, a diffusion transformer that extends the all-atom representation of Vilya-1 from modeling individual molecules to modeling their interactions with protein targets. This all-atom representation enables transfer learning between different molecular types, and delivers highly accurate structural modeling of peptides across sizes, classes, and compositions bound to therapeutically relevant targets. By generating diverse structural ensembles and ranking them with calibrated confidence, Vilya-2 recovers 59.1% of peptide interfaces to sub-2 Å backbone RMSD, far exceeding the performance of a representative co-folding model even when that model is given the bound receptor as a template. In addition, Vilya-2 is state-of-the-art at small-molecule docking, and generalizes to novel protein-small molecule complexes unlike those seen in training. It also generalizes to modeling molecular conformations of diverse macrocycles and disulfide-stapled miniproteins several-fold larger than any molecule seen in training. Finally, Vilya-2 can be used as a foundation model, and fine-tuned to enrich for active compounds in hit-to-lead campaigns. By unifying predictive accuracy with broad generalizability across chemical space, Vilya-2 is the structure-prediction oracle that de novo peptide design pipelines require--establishing the all-atom approach as a general foundation for the design and evaluation of de novo peptide therapeutics.

AI.tldr: Vilya-2 extends Vilya-1 with an all-atom diffusion transformer to model peptide–protein interactions, enabling transfer learning across molecular types. It achieves high accuracy across peptides, macrocycles, and small molecules, including state-of-the-art docking, and serves as a foundation model for de novo peptide design.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of co-evolutionary structure-prediction methods for peptide therapeutics (non-canonical residues, macrocycles, complex topologies) by adopting an all-atom representation that generalizes across molecular types and supports de novo design.
AI.method: A diffusion transformer with an all-atom representation that models interactions between peptides/proteins and targets. Enables transfer learning between molecular types, generates diverse structural ensembles, and ranks them with calibrated confidence. Can be fine-tuned to enrich for actives in hit-to-lead campaigns.
AI.result: Recovered 59.1% of peptide interfaces to sub-2 Å backbone RMSD, outperforming a representative co-folding model even with the bound receptor as a template. State-of-the-art docking for small molecules; generalizes to novel protein–small molecule complexes. Generalizes to macrocycles and disulfide-stapled miniproteins larger than training. Can serve as a foundation model and be fine-tuned to enrich for actives in hit-to-lead campaigns.
AI.conclusion: An all-atom approach provides a general foundation for de novo peptide therapeutics design and evaluation, elevating predictive accuracy and broad generalizability across chemical space; Vilya-2 functions as a structure-prediction oracle for de novo peptide design pipelines.

title: Cooperative Multi-UAV Navigation in Complex Environments via Systematic Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Cooperative navigation of multi-agent UAVs in complex environments faces key challenges including local optima traps, sparse rewards, learning imbalance among agents, and insufficient cross-scenario generalisation. This paper proposes a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework that addresses these issues through coordinated exploration, demonstration exploitation, safe curriculum scheduling, and structure-aware generalisation. First, a perception mechanism combining memory of visited states, directional novelty estimates, and penalty backpropagation enables agents to proactively detect and escape local optima. Second, a hierarchical collaborative demonstration buffer with tiered behaviour cloning manages trajectories by degree of team collaboration and applies differential supervision to the actor network, improving demonstration utilisation under sparse collaborative signals. Third, a safety-aware dual-condition curriculum scheduling mechanism reviews mastered scenarios through back-testing and experience pre-filling during training, suppressing catastrophic forgetting while ensuring both task performance and flight safety. For generalisation, local geometric features computed from sensor readings are abstracted into a domain parameter, through which a structure-aware gating network and mixture-of-experts mechanism condition the policy on local structural patterns rather than scenario-specific coordinates, enabling cross-scenario transfer without exposure to the target environment. The framework is further validated under mixed static-dynamic obstacle settings, showing robust adaptability to dynamic disturbances. Simulation results confirm strong performance in collaboration success rate, navigation robustness, zero-shot cross-scenario generalisation, and dynamic environment adaptability.

AI.tldr: A multi-agent UAV DRL framework with coordinated exploration, demonstration exploitation, safety-aware curriculum, and structure-aware generalization; demonstrates zero-shot cross-scenario generalization and robustness in mixed static-dynamic environments.
AI.motivation: To overcome key challenges in cooperative UAV navigation: local optima entrapment, sparse rewards, imbalanced learning among agents, and poor cross-scenario generalization.
AI.method: 1) Perception: memory of visited states, directional novelty estimates, and penalty backpropagation to proactively detect/escape local optima. 2) Hierarchical collaborative demonstration buffer: tiered behavior cloning by degree of team collaboration with differential supervision to the actor network for efficient use of sparse collaborative signals. 3) Safety-aware dual-condition curriculum scheduling: back-testing mastered scenarios and experience pre-filling to suppress forgetting while ensuring task performance and flight safety. 4) Generalization: abstract local geometric features from sensors into a domain parameter; structure-aware gating network and mixture-of-experts condition policy on local structural patterns rather than coordinates for cross-scenario transfer. 5) Validation in mixed static-dynamic obstacles to show robustness to disturbances.
AI.result: The framework achieves high collaboration success rate, improved navigation robustness, zero-shot cross-scenario generalization, and strong adaptability to dynamic environments in simulations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively mitigates local optima, sparse rewards, collaboration learning imbalance, and cross-scenario generalization gaps in cooperative UAV navigation, delivering strong zero-shot transfer and safety-conscious performance; future work could extend to real-world experiments and broader obstacle types.

title: GLIDE: Guided Layerwise Hybrid Attention for Efficient LLM Inference
summary: As Large Language Models scale to increasingly long contexts, the memory I/O and computational overhead of the Key-Value (KV) cache during decoding emerges as the primary throughput bottleneck. To address this, we propose GLIDE, a Guided Layerwise Hybrid Attention that strategically integrates sliding-window softmax attention with linear recurrent aggregation. GLIDE is motivated by layer-wise heterogeneity: early layers exhibit high sensitivity to softmax removal, while deeper layers demonstrate redundancy and tolerate aggressive replacement by linear alternatives. Leveraging this insight, GLIDE introduces a layer-wise adaptive mechanism wherein each layer balances an efficient linear recurrence with a variable-sized softmax window. Unlike uniform hybrid approaches, GLIDE non-uniformly compresses the softmax footprint across the model, reducing aggregate KV cache I/O while preserving expressive power where most vital. Empirical evaluations demonstrate the GLIDE achieves superior performance-efficiency tradeoffs, reducing end-to-end latency for long-context generation without compromising quality.

AI.tldr: GLIDE reduces KV-cache I/O and latency in long-context decoding by a layer-wise adaptive hybrid attention that combines sliding-window softmax attention with linear recurrent aggregation, applied non-uniformly across layers.
AI.motivation: As LLMs scale to longer contexts, KV-cache memory I/O and compute become the main throughput bottleneck during decoding; a more efficient attention mechanism is needed without sacrificing quality.
AI.method: GLIDE introduces Guided Layerwise Hybrid Attention: per-layer adaptive balance between a linear recurrent aggregation and a variable-sized sliding-window softmax attention. Early layers retain softmax sensitivity; deeper layers rely more on linear recurrence. The softmax footprint (window size) is non-uniformly compressed across layers to reduce KV-cache I/O while preserving critical expressive power. This integrates sliding-window attention with linear recurrence in a layer-wise fashion.
AI.result: Empirical results show GLIDE achieves better performance-efficiency tradeoffs, reducing end-to-end latency for long-context generation without noticeable quality loss (preserving generation quality while lowering latency and memory I/O).
AI.conclusion: GLIDE offers a scalable, layer-aware approach to long-context decoding that reduces KV-cache I/O and latency while maintaining generation quality, outperforming uniform hybrid methods.

title: Medical world models in healthcare: foundations, applications, and challenges for trustworthy clinical translation
summary: Medical world models offer a framework for extending medical artificial intelligence beyond static prediction by representing evolving patient states and modelling how they change over time and in response to clinical interventions. This Review defines the conceptual boundaries, technical foundations, application domains, and evidence requirements of the field through a structured narrative synthesis with reproducible evidence mapping.We screened 1,455 unique records and assembled a corpus of 98 sources, including 14 studies that met a strict empirical definition of a medical world model. The field is organised around four capabilities: patient state representation, temporal dynamics modelling, intervention-conditioned simulation, and clinician-supervised planning. Evidence spans medical imaging, longitudinal electronic health records, treatment response modelling, physiological and multimodal state modelling, ultrasound and surgical interaction, and population and health-system simulation; clinical digital twins are treated as a cross-cutting integration framework.Current studies provide early evidence of technical feasibility for trajectory forecasting and comparison of candidate interventions, but most remain retrospective, task-specific, or preclinical. The evidence base is further limited by incomplete longitudinal intervention data, inconsistent action semantics, limited causal identifiability, long-horizon error accumulation, inadequate uncertainty estimation, and limited external validation. Clinical translation will therefore depend on precise intervention representations, robust causal and mechanistic grounding, calibrated trajectory-level uncertainty, safety-constrained planning, and prospective multicentre validation against clinically meaningful endpoints.

AI.tldr: Medical world models show promise for dynamic patient-state modelling and intervention-conditioned planning, but the evidence is early and limited by data quality, causality, uncertainty, and external validation.
AI.motivation: To define the boundaries, foundations, domains, and evidence requirements of medical world models and to map the evidence base.
AI.method: Structured narrative synthesis with reproducible evidence mapping; screened 1,455 records; assembled 98 sources; 14 empirical studies met a strict empirical definition.
AI.result: Field centers on four capabilities: (1) patient state representation, (2) temporal dynamics modelling, (3) intervention-conditioned simulation, (4) clinician-supervised planning. Evidence spans medical imaging, longitudinal EHRs, treatment-response modelling, physiological and multimodal state modelling, ultrasound/surgical interaction, and population/health-system simulation. Clinical digital twins are a cross-cutting integration framework. Early technical feasibility for trajectory forecasting and intervention comparison; but most work is retrospective, task-specific, or preclinical. Limitations include incomplete longitudinal intervention data, inconsistent action semantics, limited causal identifiability, long-horizon error accumulation, inadequate uncertainty estimation, and limited external validation.
AI.conclusion: Clinical translation will require precise intervention representations, robust causal/mechanistic grounding, calibrated trajectory-level uncertainty, safety-constrained planning, and prospective multicentre validation against clinically meaningful endpoints.

title: CondPSE: A Polynomial-Filtered Structural Encoder with Conditional Modulation for Graphs
comment: Accepted as a poster at the 2nd Frontiers in Graph Machine Learning for the Large Model Era (GMLLM'26), a KDD 2026 workshop
summary: Message-passing graph neural networks are bounded by the 1-WL test and can miss topological structure that distinguishes non-isomorphic graphs. Positional and structural encodings (PSE) inject such topology-derived signals, and learned PSE encoders such as GPSE pretrain a single encoder to produce these signals from random node probes, which can then be frozen and reused as inputs across downstream graph models. We present CondPSE, a learned PSE encoder that applies a learnable polynomial graph filter bank to standard Gaussian node probes and refines the resulting structural-response branches through FiLM-style modulation conditioned on cross-filter, local message-passing, and graph-level signals. CondPSE is pretrained to reconstruct node-level positional/structural targets and graph-level invariants, and is then frozen for use as a downstream input encoding. On synthetic structural-discrimination benchmarks, CondPSE separates graph structures that 1-WL-bounded message passing cannot: it raises CSL accuracy from 42.9% to 97.3% and EXP accuracy from 68.3% to 99.9% relative to GPSE, and ablations show that the polynomial filter bank accounts for most of this gain. On real molecular property prediction, the picture is more limited. With a hybrid local-message-passing/global-attention backbone, CondPSE performs comparably to GPSE without surpassing it, and a ZINC backbone sweep shows no consistent ordering between the two encoders. We report these results and discuss why strong synthetic structural discrimination does not, on its own, yield a downstream advantage for frozen learned PSE encoders, including the role of downstream integration and possible mismatch between structural pretraining targets and molecular property labels.

AI.tldr: CondPSE introduces a learnable polynomial graph-filter bank to generate positional/structural encodings from Gaussian probes, pretraining to reconstruct node-level and graph-level targets, then freezing the encoder for downstream usage. It achieves strong synthetic topological discrimination beyond GPSE but shows limited, task-dependent gains on real molecular prediction, highlighting downstream integration and target mismatch issues.
AI.motivation: To overcome the 1-WL limitation of message-passing GNNs by learning robust positional/structural encodings (PSE) that can be frozen and reused across models, and to evaluate whether stronger synthetic structural discrimination translates to downstream gains.
AI.method: A learnable polynomial graph-filter bank processes standard Gaussian node probes. FiLM-style modulation refines the resulting structural branches conditioned on cross-filter signals, local message-passing, and graph-level cues. The encoder is pretrained to reconstruct node-level positional/structural targets and graph invariants, then frozen for downstream encoding.
AI.result: On synthetic benchmarks, CondPSE substantially outperforms GPSE in discriminating structures that 1-WL-bounded MPNNs miss (CSL: 42.9%→97.3%; EXP: 68.3%→99.9%; ablations show the polynomial filter bank drives most gains). On real molecular tasks with a hybrid local-message-passing/global-attention backbone, CondPSE matches but does not surpass GPSE; a ZINC backbone sweep reveals no consistent ordering between the encoders.
AI.conclusion: Strong synthetic discriminability from a frozen learned PSE encoder does not automatically yield downstream advantages; benefits depend on how well the pretraining targets align with downstream tasks and how integration with the downstream model is performed. The work discusses potential mismatch between structural pretraining targets and molecular property labels and emphasizes downstream design as a key factor for transfer.

title: Tripody: An Overconstrained 3-SPR-like Parallel Robot for High-Reach Construction Tasks
comment: 8 pages, 11 figures, Accepted in July 2026 at IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)
summary: Many ceiling construction tasks still rely on heavy serial manipulators that are difficult to deploy in cluttered interiors, motivating lightweight, field-ready alternatives that reach ceiling height while maintaining millimeter-level accuracy and the stiffness demanded by overhead tool loads. We introduce Tripody, a wheeled 3-DoF parallel robot for high-reach tasks that replaces the base spherical joints of a classical 3-SPR (3 legs; S: base spherical joint; P: actuated prismatic joint; R: end-effector revolute joint) morphology with universal joints, intentionally overconstraining the mechanism; small, distributed elastic deflections absorb the resulting incompatibilities, preserving predominantly translational motion. The 33kg system extends from 1.7m to 3.4m in height, supports a continuous 32kg payload, and offers a modular end-effector interface for ceiling operations. We detail the mechanical design - including custom linear actuators and a kinematic-compatibility analysis - and a control stack for accurate positioning that combines SE(3) state estimation, forward kinematics, and task-space control. In experiments, Tripody exhibits similar in-plane stiffness to a spherical-base variant but substantially higher torsional stiffness - an increase of 67% at 1.7m, 196% at 2.6m, and 454% at 3.4m - while maintaining negligible cross-axis coupling. Closed-loop positioning with a total station converges below 0.6mm across the entire workspace; pure model extrapolation achieves a 95th-percentile error of 2.7mm (max 3.6mm). Finally, we demonstrate task-level ceiling-drilling feasibility in an open-loop study by drilling a 15-hole pattern with 4.5mm maximum relative hole-position error after rigid alignment. These results support overconstrained, compliance-absorbing 3-SPR-like architectures as a practical path to lightweight, high- reach, millimeter-accurate construction robots.

AI.tldr: Tripody is a lightweight, high-reach 3-DoF parallel robot that overconstrains a 3-SPR-like architecture with universal joints and elastic deflections to absorb incompatibilities, achieving millimeter-accuracy and high torsional stiffness for ceiling tasks.
AI.motivation: To enable ceiling construction and maintenance tasks with a lightweight, field-ready platform that maintains millimeter-level positioning accuracy and stiffness under overhead loads, addressing the limitations of heavy serial manipulators in cluttered interiors.
AI.method: Replace base spherical joints in a 3-SPR with universal joints to create an overconstrained mechanism; introduce distributed elastic deflections to absorb incompatibilities; build a 33 kg, height-extending system (1.7–3.4 m) with modular end-effectors and custom linear actuators; develop a control stack using SE(3) state estimation, forward kinematics, and task-space control; perform stiffness measurements, closed-loop positioning with a total station (<0.6 mm), model extrapolation predicts 95th percentile error of 2.7 mm (max 3.6 mm), and demonstrate ceiling drilling with 4.5 mm hole-position error after rigid alignment.
AI.result: The system achieves in-plane stiffness comparable to a spherical-base variant but with substantially higher torsional stiffness (increases of 67%, 196%, 454% at 1.7, 2.6, and 3.4 m respectively); cross-axis coupling remains negligible; closed-loop positioning converges under 0.6 mm; pure-model extrapolation yields 95th percentile error of 2.7 mm (max 3.6 mm); open-loop drilling tests show 15-hole pattern with ≤4.5 mm relative hole-position error after alignment.
AI.conclusion: Overconstrained, compliance-absorbing 3-SPR-like architectures are a practical path toward lightweight, high-reach, millimeter-accurate construction robots for ceiling tasks.

title: A GAN-Based Framework for Robust Data Synthesis in Satellite Internet Observations
comment: This paper has been accepted by the IEEE International Symposium on Personal, Indoor and Mobile Radio Communications 2026 (PIMRC 2026), 1 - 4 September 2026, Singapore
summary: Low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite Internet has become an important infrastructure for enabling ubiquitous connectivity to align with the International Telecommunications Union vision for 6G telecommunications networks. However, current LEO satellite Internet observations often suffer from missing data, which complicates data augmentation task and limits the expansion of representative datasets. Given the complex characteristics of these datasets, generative AI (GenAI) presents a promising approach, yet its application in this domain has received little attention to date. In this paper, we propose a GenAI-based framework to synthesize high-fidelity data directly from incomplete LEO network observations. We propose the representative data missing scenarios, and evaluate the performance with the latest GAN- and VAE-based GenAI models on the recent WetLinks dataset. We design block-wise and point-wise missing scenarios to closely simulate the data loss that happens on real-world LEO satellite networks. Our results show the effectiveness of our proposed GAN-based framework and GT-GAN model exhibits the best performance among all models in both missing scenarios. Even under extreme conditions (e.g., 40% of the input data is missing), GT-GAN shows the highest robustness, consistently capturing the underlying input data distribution and being the least affected in terms of generalization. Our results shed light on future directions for GenAI-based data augmentation methods and data-driven research on satellite network measurement.

AI.tldr: A GenAI-based framework synthesizes high-fidelity data from incomplete LEO network observations; GT-GAN achieves top performance under missing data scenarios, showing robustness and potential for data augmentation in satellite network measurement.
AI.motivation: Missing data in LEO satellite Internet observations hampers data augmentation and dataset expansion. GenAI offers a promising remedy but has been underexplored in this domain; evaluating on WetLinks with realistic missingness to guide future data-driven research.
AI.method: Introduce representative missing scenarios (block-wise and point-wise) to simulate real-world data loss. Compare recent GAN- and VAE-based GenAI models on WetLinks. Implement a GAN-based framework with GT-GAN and assess performance across missingness levels, focusing on reconstruction fidelity and generalization.
AI.result: GT-GAN outperforms all competing models in both missing scenarios and maintains robustness under extreme missingness (up to 40% missing). It best captures the underlying input distribution and shows the least degradation in generalization, indicating strong suitability for data augmentation in satellite networks.
AI.conclusion: GenAI-based data augmentation for satellite network measurement is promising, with GT-GAN offering robust, high-fidelity synthesis under missing data. This work motivates further development of GenAI methods tailored to satellite data and broader data-driven, measurement-oriented research in LEO networks.

title: FORGE: Frame Orthogonality in Relevance Geometry for Long-Form Video Understanding
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled long-form video understanding at a scale that was not previously possible. However, the density of relevant content decreases sharply as video sequence length increases, and exposing the model to more irrelevant content measurably reduces its accuracy. In this paper, we address the problem of maximizing query-relevant information in a frame subset selected at inference time, without training. FORGE (Frame Orthogonality in Relevance Geometry) is a model-agnostic method that induces a query-conditioned geometry on a pretrained multimodal embedding space, unifying relevance and diversity into a single objective. In this space, frames that cover independent query-relevant directions are far apart, and selecting the subset of maximum information captures diverse query-relevant content within the budget. Experiments on Video-MME and LongVideoBench at budgets of 16, 32, and 64 frames show that FORGE improves the unified keyframe selection score by 11.0-15.3 points over the strongest training-free baseline and up to doubles keyframe recall (0.415 vs. 0.204 at K=64 on Video-MME). The gains extend to question answering, where accuracy improves in every evaluated setting across eight open-source MLLMs spanning 4B to 32B parameters, by up to 8.7 points over uniform sampling and 5.2 points over the strongest baseline. Our findings suggest that aligning the embedding space with the query's high-dimensional structure is a promising direction for inference-time video understanding.

AI.tldr: FORGE is a training-free, model-agnostic frame-selection method for multimodal LLMs that maximizes query-relevant information in long videos by selecting frames that span independent query-relevant directions in a pretrained embedding space, balancing relevance and diversity.
AI.motivation: Long-form videos contain many irrelevant frames; to improve inference without fine-tuning, there is a need to select a compact, information-rich subset that preserves query relevance.
AI.method: FORGE induces a query-conditioned geometry (Frame Orthogonality in Relevance Geometry) in a pretrained multimodal embedding space and formulates a single objective that renders frames covering independent query-relevant directions far apart. At inference, it selects a budgeted subset (e.g., 16/32/64) without training, maximizing information coverage.
AI.result: On Video-MME and LongVideoBench (K=16/32/64), FORGE improves the unified keyframe selection score by 11.0–15.3 points vs strongest training-free baseline and doubles keyframe recall (0.415 vs 0.204 at K=64 on Video-MME). In QA, across eight open-source MLLMs (4B–32B parameters), accuracy improves by up to 8.7 points vs uniform sampling and 5.2 points vs strongest baseline.
AI.conclusion: Aligning the embedding space with the query's high-dimensional structure is a promising direction for inference-time video understanding; FORGE provides a simple, model-agnostic, training-free mechanism to balance relevance and diversity in frame selection.

title: Rethinking CD: A Reproducibility Study and Extension on the Ineffectiveness of Contrastive Decoding at Mitigating Object Hallucinations in MLLMs
summary: Contrastive decoding (CD) has been proposed as a training-free strategy for mitigating object hallucinations in multimodal large language models (MLLMs), with reported gains on benchmarks such as POPE. However, recent work has questioned whether these gains reflect genuine improvements in visual grounding. In this study, we reproduce and extend the findings of "The Mirage of Performance Gains: Why Contrastive Decoding Fails to Mitigate Object Hallucinations in MLLMs." Specifically, we test the claim that CD induces a unidirectional output distribution shift in discriminative datasets and examine its generalizability across datasets. We also verify that the adaptive plausibility constraint (APC) reduces sampling to greedy search on both discriminative and generative benchmarks. Beyond reproduction, we rigorously study the effects of CD across generative and discriminative datasets. We conduct several experiments that provide additional insights: we analyze the logit distributions induced by different CD strategies on generative datasets, propose a proxy method and compare its performance against CD techniques, and investigate how hallucination signals propagate through each layer of the expert and amateur models. Experimental results across MME, POPE, and CHAIR using LLaVA and Qwen validate the original claims and show that the apparent improvements from CD are often spurious and do not consistently translate into stronger visual grounding for reducing hallucinations. These findings challenge the effectiveness of current contrastive decoding strategies and motivate the development of more reliable approaches for mitigating hallucinations in MLLMs.

AI.tldr: Reproducing and extending contrastive decoding (CD) claims in multimodal LLMs reveals that reported gains in reducing object hallucinations are often spurious; APC collapses sampling to greedy search; findings generalize across datasets but do not consistently improve visual grounding; a proxy method is proposed for comparison and results emphasize the need for more reliable mitigation strategies.
AI.motivation: Question whether CD genuinely improves visual grounding in MLLMs and whether reported gains reflect true reductions in object hallucinations. Test claims of unidirectional logit shifts on discriminative data, assess generalizability across datasets, and examine the adaptive plausibility constraint (APC) effect.
AI.method: Reproduce prior CD experiments on discriminative and generative benchmarks (MME, POPE, CHAIR) using LLaVA and Qwen. Analyze logit distributions under different CD strategies, verify APC’s effect (reducing sampling to greedy search), propose a proxy method and compare with CD, and study how hallucination signals propagate through expert and amateur model layers.
AI.result: Experiments corroborate that CD-induced improvements are often spurious and do not consistently yield stronger visual grounding. APC reduces sampling to greedy search on both discriminative and generative benchmarks. Across MME, POPE, and CHAIR with LLaVA and Qwen, results align with prior claims about unidirectional distribution shifts on discriminative data and show limited generalization; a proxy method can match or exceed some CD effects but overall gains remain unreliable.
AI.conclusion: Current contrastive decoding strategies are not reliably effective at mitigating hallucinations in MLLMs. The findings highlight the fragility and non-generalizability of CD-driven gains and motivate the development of more robust, proven methods for improving visual grounding in multimodal models.

title: Motion-Acceleration Calibration and Compensation in IMUs without External Equipment for Attitude Estimation Filters
summary:
Attitude estimation based on inertial sensing requires measurements of local angular velocities and local gravity via gyroscopes and accelerometers.
  However, during the motion of a mobile system the inertial measurement unit (IMU) will be subject to additional accelerations which skews the measurement of local gravity.
  This effect gets amplified the further away the IMU is from the base of the system.
  Many attitude estimation filters, such as "Madgwick" or "Mahony", account for this by relying more on gyroscope integration for periods of high angular velocity.
  However, this approach is prone to accumulate long term error especially around the gravity vector.
  In this work we utilize the gyroscope measurements to compensate the additional accelerations induced by the motion of the system, i.e., centripetal- and tangential-accelerations.
  Additionally, we introduce a calibration method that estimates intrinsic IMU parameters such as axes misalignment, bias, scale, as well as the extrinsic base-to-IMU vector without the necessity for additional external equipment.
  Our evaluation in simulation as well as in the real-world shows that this method improves any attitude filter that relies on the direction of gravity.
  Furthermore we demonstrate the effectivenes on highly dynamic systems, and systems that are unable to put the IMU at the center of rotation, using our real-world spherical mobile mapping system.

AI.tldr: Use gyros to compensate motion-induced accelerations (centripetal/tangential) and perform self-contained IMU calibration (axes, bias, scale, extrinsic base-to-IMU) to improve gravity-based attitude estimation in dynamic systems, including off-center IMUs.
AI.motivation: Gravity-based attitude estimation is distorted by motion: extra accelerations from movement bias gravity measurements; off-center IMUs amplify errors; existing filters lean on gyro integration during high angular velocity, risking long-term drift. A compensation and self-calibration approach can improve accuracy and robustness.
AI.method: Leverage gyroscope data to counteract centripetal and tangential accelerations caused by motion and develop a calibration framework that jointly estimates intrinsic IMU parameters (axes misalignment, bias, scale) and extrinsic base-to-IMU vector without external equipment.
AI.result: Simulation and real-world experiments show improved performance of gravity-based attitude filters due to the compensation and calibration method. The method is effective in highly dynamic systems and when the IMU is not at the rotation center, demonstrated on a real spherical mobile mapping system.
AI.conclusion: The approach enhances robustness and accuracy of gravity-direction based attitude estimation under dynamic motion and offset conditions, enabling self-contained calibration suitable for challenging deployments.

title: Reasoning with Memory: A Temporal Granularity-Adaptive Framework for Training-Free Long Video Understanding
summary: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) demonstrate superior generalization in fundamental video tasks, restricted context windows limit their long video understanding. To accommodate this constraint, models typically resort to keyframe selection. However, uniform sampling or static query-guided selection often overlooks critical temporal context, failing to adapt to the varying query temporal granularities. In this paper, we propose ReMem, a temporal granularity-adaptive keyframe selection framework for training-free LongVideoQA. ReMem introduces a dual-level memory-augmented adaptation. At the query level, Memory-Driven Question Parsing leverages LLM long-term memory to decode question temporal granularity and extract semantic entities. At the video level, Synergistic Dual-Semantic Frame Alignment exploits intrinsic structural memory to align frames with query semantics, guiding Structure-Aware Dynamic Frame Routing to cluster events and optimally distribute sampling budgets. By explicitly preserving temporal information with memory mechanisms, ReMem suppresses redundancy and empowers MLLMs to perform robust multi-granular video reasoning. Evaluations across four popular LongVideoQA benchmarks using three MLLMs demonstrate highly efficient, state-of-the-art zero-shot performance; notably, LLaVA-Video with ReMem reaches 54.5% (+12.3%) on LVBench and 67.1% (+8.2%) on LongVideoBench.

AI.tldr: ReMem is a training-free, memory-augmented framework for LongVideoQA that adaptively selects keyframes via dual-level memory, achieving state-of-the-art zero-shot performance across four benchmarks (e.g., LLaVA-Video + ReMem: 54.5% on LVBench, 67.1% on LongVideoBench).
AI.motivation: Long video understanding is constrained by limited context windows in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Uniform or static keyframe sampling fails to capture critical temporal context and cannot adapt to different query granularities. A memory-augmented, adaptive approach is proposed to preserve temporal information and enable multi-granular reasoning.
AI.method: Dual-level memory-augmented adaptation: (1) Query level — Memory-Driven Question Parsing uses long-term memory of LLMs to decode the question’s temporal granularity and extract semantic entities. (2) Video level — Synergistic Dual-Semantic Frame Alignment leverages intrinsic structural memory to align frames with query semantics, guiding Structure-Aware Dynamic Frame Routing to cluster events and allocate sampling budgets.
AI.result: Evaluations on four LongVideoQA benchmarks with three MLLMs show strong zero-shot performance and efficiency. Notably, LLaVA-Video with ReMem achieves 54.5% (+12.3%) on LVBench and 67.1% (+8.2%) on LongVideoBench.
AI.conclusion: Memory-augmented design preserves temporal information, reduces redundancy, and enables robust multi-granular video reasoning in a training-free manner, achieving state-of-the-art zero-shot results across benchmarks.

title: ScaleResfusion: Residual Rectified Flow based on Residual Vector Field
summary: Real-world Image Restoration (Real-IR) aims to recover high-quality (HQ) images from complex and unknown degradations. Although recent diffusion-based methods have substantially improved perceptual quality, their current designs leave two key challenges unresolved. Methods that start from Gaussian noise are slow and often less faithful to the degraded input. Residual-based methods usually train from scratch, which makes it hard to exploit modern pre-trained generative priors. In this paper, we present ScaleResfusion, a scalable diffusion framework for real-world image restoration built on pre-trained text-to-image rectified-flow models. The core of our method is Residual Rectified Flow, which introduces the residual term R into Standard Rectified Flow. Instead of starting from pure noise, it uses a residual transport path that starts from noisy low-quality (LQ) images and admits an exact acceleration point. By learning the residual vector field, Residual Rectified Flow keeps the output distribution and linear diffusion process consistent with the pre-trained rectified-flow models. This makes parameter-efficient fine-tuning possible at scale. We further introduce a knowledge-distillation pipeline to reduce sampling cost while maintaining restoration quality. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world restoration tasks show that ScaleResfusion achieves state-of-the-art performance with much higher efficiency. These results suggest a practical and scalable way to adapt large pre-trained diffusion models to real-world image restoration. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/YukinoshitaLove/ScaleResfusion.

AI.tldr: ScaleResfusion extends rectified-flow diffusion with a residual term to enable efficient, fine-tunable real-world image restoration using pre-trained priors, achieving faster sampling and state-of-the-art performance.
AI.motivation: Real-world image restoration suffers from unknown degradations; diffusion-based methods are slow and may not leverage pre-trained priors. There is a need for scalable, parameter-efficient adaptation of large diffusion models to restoration tasks.
AI.method: Introduce Residual Rectified Flow by adding a residual vector field R to standard rectified flow. Start the diffusion process from noisy low-quality (LQ) images with an exact acceleration point, learning the residual to maintain consistency with pre-trained rectified-flow models. This enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning at scale. A knowledge-distillation pipeline reduces sampling cost. Built on pre-trained text-to-image rectified-flow models.
AI.result: Empirically achieves state-of-the-art restoration performance with higher efficiency across multiple real-world restoration tasks; demonstrates practical scalability and provides code for reproduction.
AI.conclusion: ScaleResfusion offers a practical and scalable framework for adapting large pre-trained diffusion models to real-world image restoration, combining residual rectified flow with efficient distillation for improved speed and fidelity.

title: Algorithmic Separation between Constant-Depth and Logarithmic-Depth Neural Networks
summary:
Despite the empirical advantages of deep networks over shallow ones, theoretical depth separations largely concern approximation power, while algorithmic results are mostly limited to comparisons between two- and three-layer networks. In this work, we prove the first algorithmic separation between constant-depth and logarithmic-depth networks.
  Specifically, we identify a class of Boolean functions with hierarchically structured Fourier spectra that logarithmic-depth networks can learn efficiently using layerwise coordinate descent by reconstructing the spectra hierarchically and adaptively. We also exhibit a subclass for which every constant-depth, polynomial-width network with sufficiently regular activations and controlled spectral norms must incur constant $L^2$ approximation error under the uniform distribution over the hypercube.

AI.tldr: First algorithmic separation between constant-depth and logarithmic-depth networks: log-depth nets learn certain Boolean functions via layerwise coordinate descent; some constant-depth nets with regular activations and bounded spectral norms cannot achieve small L2 error on uniform hypercube distribution.
AI.motivation: Address the gap between theoretical depth separations (approximation power) and algorithmic results; extend depth separation to learning algorithms beyond two-/three-layer comparisons; show concrete tasks where depth helps in learning.
AI.method: Define a class of Boolean functions with hierarchically structured Fourier spectra; develop a layerwise coordinate descent algorithm that reconstructs spectra in a hierarchical, adaptive manner for log-depth networks; define a subclass where constant-depth, polynomial-width networks with regular activations and spectral norm control fail to approximate beyond a constant error under the uniform distribution.
AI.result: Efficient learning with log-depth networks via the proposed algorithm; demonstration of a constant-depth network limitation for the subclass, yielding constant L2 error under the uniform distribution; establishes an algorithmic depth separation.
AI.conclusion: Provides the first algorithmic depth separation between constant-depth and logarithmic-depth networks; supports the view that depth adds computational advantages for learning structured functions; clarifies limits of shallow architectures under spectral-norm constraints.

title: Transformer Transformer: A Unified Model for Motion-Conditioned Robot Co-design
comment: 26 pages, 12 figures, 20 tables. Project page: https://transformer-transformer.github.io
summary: An often overlooked factor of robot manipulation performance is the embodiment of the robot itself. Motivated by this problem, we study motion-conditioned robot co-design, where the goal is to generate complete robot designs that track target end-effector trajectories (from human demonstrations) while optimizing user-defined rewards. We introduce Transformer Transformer, a diffusion transformer trained on RoboTokens, a unified tokenization of robot embodiments, states, and actions. The same architecture can be used across embodiment spaces (e.g., wheeled bimanual, quadrupeds, humanoids) and use cases (embodiment generation, cross embodiment controller). Rather than overfitting to one reward function, Transformer Transformer is a dynamics model, whose reward-agnostic state and action predictions can be converted into reward-specific value predictions. These value predictions are used to steer embodiment diffusion towards high value robot designs, through a procedure we call Dynamics Self-Guidance. Experiments across multiple design spaces show zero-shot optimization of unseen rewards and trajectories, improving performance and runtime over the evolutionary baseline. Finally, we fabricated an optimized ALOHA design, which reduced tracking error by over 70% compared to the original design.

AI.tldr: A diffusion-based, reward-agnostic, cross-embodiment robot co-design framework that uses Dynamics Self-Guidance to optimize designs for target trajectories across multiple embodiment spaces, validated by zero-shot reward optimization and a fabricatable ALOHA design with large tracking-error improvements.
AI.motivation: Embodiment has a critical, often underappreciated impact on robot manipulation; existing design methods struggle to generalize across embodiments and tasks and rely on slow, reward-specific optimization. A unified dynamics model across embodiments can enable efficient, zero-shot design optimization.
AI.method: Introduce Transformer Transformer, a diffusion Transformer trained on RoboTokens (tokenized embodiments, states, actions). The model operates across embodiment spaces and use cases; it functions as a dynamics model with reward-agnostic predictions that can be converted to reward-specific value predictions. Dynamics Self-Guidance steers the diffusion process toward high-value designs by leveraging these values.
AI.result: Demonstrates zero-shot optimization of unseen rewards and trajectories across multiple design spaces, outperforming an evolutionary baseline in both performance and runtime. Fabricated an optimized ALOHA design achieving >70% reduction in tracking error compared to the original design.
AI.conclusion: A unified dynamics-model approach with reward-agnostic predictions enables efficient cross-embodiment co-design via Dynamics Self-Guidance. The framework generalizes to diverse embodiment spaces and use cases, with tangible performance gains and a successful fabrication example.

title: When Shortest Isn't Safest: A Design Science Approach to Senior-Friendly Pedestrian Routing
summary: Older adults' independent mobility enables out-of-home participation, well-being and health, yet pedestrian navigation systems still optimize primarily for distance or time, often overlooking barriers, safety thresholds, and supportive infrastructure that shape late-life walking decisions. We present a senior-friendly pedestrian routing artefact developed through echeloned Design Science Re-search, translating lived mobility constraints into prescriptive design knowledge. Based on 11 semi-structured interviews, we derive initial Design Requirements (DRs) and Design Principles (DPs) for barrier-aware, amenity-sensitive routing and execution-relevant explanations. We instantiate these in an OpenStreetMap pedestrian network enriched with amenities (benches, toilets, and shelters) and height data, and implemented an A*-based routing engine with configurable costs and explanation payloads. In a field-based walking study, 14 older adults com-pared artefact-generated routes with baselines and provided ratings and qualitative feedback; the senior-friendly route was preferred overall. Thematic analysis further showed that infrastructure maintenance, seasonal conditions, traffic exposure, and social context shape route acceptance. We synthesize these insights into refined DRs and DPs emphasizing context-aware hazard modeling, multi-route transparency, landmark-grounded explanations, social-context sensitivity, and stage-appropriate information. Our contributions provide actionable guidance for practitioners developing senior-friendly pedestrian navigation systems.

AI.tldr: Senior-friendly pedestrian routing artefact enhances route choice through barrier-aware, amenity-sensitive routing with explainable guidance, validated via interviews and field study with older adults.
AI.motivation: Current pedestrian routing emphasizes distance/time and often overlooks late-life barriers, safety thresholds, and supportive infrastructure, hindering independent mobility of older adults.
AI.method: A Design Science Research approach: 11 semi-structured interviews to derive Design Requirements (DRs) and Design Principles (DPs); OpenStreetMap enrichment with amenities (benches, toilets, shelters) and height data; A*-based routing with configurable costs and explanation payloads; field study with 14 older adults comparing artefact-generated routes to baselines; thematic analysis to refine DRs/DPs.
AI.result: Artefact-generated routes were preferred overall; insights highlight infrastructure maintenance, seasonal conditions, traffic exposure, and social context as determinants of route acceptance; refined DRs/DPs emphasize context-aware hazard modeling, multi-route transparency, landmark-based explanations, social-context sensitivity, and stage-appropriate information.
AI.conclusion: Provides actionable guidance for practitioners developing senior-friendly pedestrian navigation systems and demonstrates the viability and acceptance of barrier-aware, amenity-sensitive routing for late-life mobility.

title: FunnelAL: Retrieve-then-Rank Active Learning for Single-Class Discovery
summary: We present FunnelAL, a retrieve-then-rank active learning system for single-class discovery, which adapts the multi-stage funnel architecture of industrial recommender systems to data annotation. Large-scale supervised learning faces two challenges: efficiently finding relevant samples in a massive corpus, and distinguishing true positives from visually confusable negatives when embeddings do not cleanly separate classes. Conventional active learning offers a principled framework for reducing annotation cost, yet it treats sample selection as a single-stage process that addresses neither challenge efficiently. FunnelAL decomposes the problem into cascaded stages. Starting from a single positive and negative example, the system iterates through: (1) embedding-based retrieval scoring that narrows the corpus to a manageable candidate set; (2) a precision-triggered ranking stage that exploits a learned ranker (RankNet) while batch precision remains high, then automatically blends in committee-based exploration (QBC) once returns diminish; and (3) feedback from the annotator's labels that refines both stages in subsequent iterations. We evaluate on three diverse image classification benchmarks. With a perfect annotator, FunnelAL attains the best final F1 on all three benchmarks, the best annotation efficiency (first in AULC), and the fewest annotation rounds. The most recent single-class discovery methods (GAL, PF-MA) at best match its final quality, and only at consistently higher labeling cost. Under annotator labeling errors at realistic rates, FunnelAL remains first or statistically tied for first while classical uncertainty-based methods degrade two to three times faster. Our work provides a concrete bridge between multi-stage recommender systems and active learning.

AI.tldr: FunnelAL is a retrieve-then-rank active learning system with a multi-stage funnel architecture for single-class discovery. It improves annotation efficiency and robustness to label noise by cascading embedding-based retrieval, precision-driven ranking with RankNet plus QBC exploration, and incremental annotator feedback; it outperforms recent methods GAL, PF-MA and uncertainty-based baselines on three image benchmarks.
AI.motivation: To efficiently find relevant samples in massive corpora and distinguish true positives from visually confusable negatives in single-class discovery, thereby reducing annotation cost. The work also adapts the multi-stage funnel architecture from industrial recommender systems to data annotation.
AI.method: FunnelAL uses cascaded stages: (1) embedding-based retrieval to narrow the corpus; (2) a precision-triggered ranking stage using a learned RankNet to keep high batch precision, followed by committee-based exploration (QBC) when returns diminish; (3) annotator feedback to refine both stages in subsequent iterations.
AI.result: Evaluated on three diverse image classification benchmarks. With a perfect annotator, FunnelAL achieves the best final F1 on all benchmarks, the best annotation efficiency (first in AULC), and the fewest annotation rounds. The most recent single-class discovery methods (GAL, PF-MA) at best match its final quality but require higher labeling cost. Under annotator labeling errors at realistic rates, FunnelAL remains first or tied for first while classical uncertainty-based methods degrade two to three times faster.
AI.conclusion: The work bridges multi-stage recommender systems and active learning, delivering a practical, efficient, and robust pipeline for single-class discovery that outperforms state-of-the-art methods and is resilient to labeling noise.

title: A Unified Algorithmic Framework for Hybrid Reinforcement Learning in Tabular MDPs with Shifted Transition Dynamics
summary: This paper investigates a hybrid reinforcement learning setting in tabular Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), where an agent aims to learn an optimal policy by combining online interactions with a target environment and offline data from a source environment. A central challenge is that offline data may be collected from outdated environments with shifted transition dynamics, making naive integration of historical data ineffective. To address this, we propose a unified algorithmic framework featuring two algorithms: MIN-UCB-VI for regret minimization and MAX-LCB-VI for best policy identification. Both algorithms leverage fine-grained bias information to more effectively exploit offline data under general transition shifts. We provide theoretical guarantees for our framework, including both instance-dependent and independent upper bounds on regret and sub-optimality gap. Furthermore, we establish matching lower bounds to demonstrate the optimality of our approach and validate our theoretical findings through extensive experiments.

AI.tldr: Proposes a unified framework for hybrid reinforcement learning in tabular MDPs that combines online interaction with offline data from a possibly shifted source, introducing MIN-UCB-VI and MAX-LCB-VI to exploit offline data via bias information; provides regret and sub-optimality bounds, matching lower bounds, and empirical validation.
AI.motivation: Offline data from outdated environments can mislead learning when transition dynamics shift; there is a need for algorithms that effectively leverage such data while accounting for shifts to minimize regret and identify near-optimal policies.
AI.method: A unified algorithmic framework with two algorithms, MIN-UCB-VI (for regret minimization) and MAX-LCB-VI (for best policy identification). The methods use fine-grained bias information to better exploit offline data under general transition shifts, likely via value-iteration-based upper and lower confidence bounds.
AI.result: Theoretical guarantees including both instance-dependent and instance-independent upper bounds on regret and sub-optimality gap; matching lower bounds establishing optimality; comprehensive experiments validating the framework.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides optimal-ish performance for hybrid online-offline RL with shifted transitions, enabling effective use of offline data while guaranteeing provable performance bounds, and is validated empirically.

title: Modular Robotic Catheters for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair
summary: Fenestrated/Branched endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR/BEVAR) require surgeons to navigate catheters and guidewires into various branches of the abdominal aorta, before deploying stent grafts to alleviate pressure on the aneurysm. Previous clinical studies suggests that surgeons continue to struggle with vessel access using standard commercial instruments, prolonging the procedural time and inducing further complications. In this work, we present two contributions to solving this problem: 1) A bespoke 2-segment steerable catheter, consisting of 4 degrees of freedom to enhance dexterity. 2) An expandable, modular tendon-driven actuation platform that can accommodate for the redundancies introduced in our system. To fabricate the catheter, we capitalized on thermal fiber drawing, a technique that creates high-aspect ratio devices at scale, and processed the catheter with laser micro-machining to soften its tip. We evaluated the system using simulations, where we investigated the catheter's bending stiffness, then its steerability with in-vitro experiments in vascular phantoms. This handheld, robotic steerable catheter system has the potential to shorten the length of future endovascular surgeries, and give clinicians the tools to resolve challenging clinical cases.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a 2-segment, 4-DoF steerable catheter and a modular tendon-driven actuation platform, fabricated via thermal fiber drawing and laser micro-machining, evaluated through simulations and in-vitro vascular phantoms to improve navigation in FEVAR/BEVAR.
AI.motivation: Fenestrated/branched endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR/BEVAR) procedures require precise navigation of catheters into abdominal branches; conventional instruments yield access difficulties, longer procedures, and more complications.
AI.method: Development of a 2-segment steerable catheter with 4 degrees of freedom; expandable, modular tendon-driven actuation platform to handle redundancies. Fabrication via thermal fiber drawing to produce high-aspect-ratio devices, with laser micro-machining to soften the tip. Evaluation included bending stiffness simulations and in-vitro steerability tests in vascular phantoms.
AI.result: Simulations assessed bending stiffness; in-vitro experiments demonstrated steerability in vascular phantoms; the handheld robotic steerable catheter showed potential to shorten endovascular surgeries.
AI.conclusion: The proposed catheter and actuation platform offer improved dexterity for challenging FEVAR/BEVAR access, with potential for shorter procedures and broader clinical applicability, warranting further in-vivo validation and translation.

title: RRS-10K: A Multitask Vision-Language Model Benchmark for Rare Remote Sensing Image Interpretation
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general remote sensing tasks. However, their capability for rare scenes remains insufficiently understood, because existing benchmarks are dominated by common urban and rural imagery. To address this gap, we present RRS-10K, a benchmark for rare remote sensing image interpretation. RRS-10K contains 10,738 military-related remote sensing images and corresponding multiple format question-answer pairs for comprehensive evaluation. All of the images are collected from first-hand sources and organized into three capability dimensions, six sub-dimensions, and 20 leaf tasks, covering perception, reasoning, and robustness. To improve the quality of multiple-choice questions, we introduce a similarity-based distractor filtering strategy (SDFS) during benchmark construction. We further evaluate 52 representative models and show that current VLMs achieve only moderate zero-shot performance on rare remote sensing image interpretation, with clear weaknesses in visual grounding, referring segmentation, and complex semantic reasoning tasks. RRS-10K enables systematic analysis of failure modes in long-tail remote sensing interpretation and provides guidance for developing more reliable remote sensing VLMs.

AI.tldr: RRS-10K: a large benchmark of 10,738 military-related remote sensing images with 20 leaf QA tasks across perception, reasoning, and robustness; introduces SDFS for better distractors; finds current VLMs show only moderate zero-shot ability and weaknesses in grounding and complex reasoning; aims to analyze failure modes and guide improvements.
AI.motivation: There's a gap in evaluating VLMs on rare/long-tail remote sensing scenes, where current benchmarks skew toward common urban/rural imagery; need systematic evaluation to understand and improve capabilities in rare scenarios.
AI.method: Curated 10,738 high-quality, first-hand military-related remote sensing images; organized into 3 capability dimensions, 6 sub-dimensions, 20 leaf tasks; generated multiple-choice QA pairs; applied similarity-based distractor filtering to improve MCQ quality; evaluated 52 representative VLMs on zero-shot performance.
AI.result: Models show moderate zero-shot performance with clear weaknesses in visual grounding, referring segmentation, and complex semantic reasoning; SDFS improves distractor quality; dataset enables analysis of failure modes and guidance for improvements.
AI.conclusion: RRS-10K provides a systematic framework to study long-tail remote sensing interpretation and will drive development of more reliable VLMs in rare scenes.

title: CLBench-V: Evaluating Multimodal Context Learning from Grounding to Knowledge Acquisition
summary: Real-world tasks often require models to learn from task-specific context rather than relying only on pre-trained knowledge. While recent work has highlighted this capability as context learning, existing evaluations mainly focus on textual contexts. In many practical settings, however, the context to be learned from is multimodal: scientific findings are conveyed through figures and tables, financial indicators are scattered across converted reports, and spatial decisions depend on maps, scenes, or web pages. We introduce CLBench-V, a benchmark for multimodal context learning that addresses the difficulty of localizing where context use breaks down by organizing tasks around three dimensions: context grounding, new information application, and new knowledge learning. CLBench-V combines converted public benchmarks with newly constructed datasets spanning domains such as science, finance, long-document understanding, spatial reasoning, and web-based visual question answering. To reduce the cost of constructing domain-specific context-learning tasks, we further use automated construction and filtering procedures for our newly built datasets. Across 3,443 instances and six recent multimodal models, the best overall score is only 0.2847, indicating that multimodal context learning remains far from saturated. Moreover, InternVL3.5-30B-A3B performs best on context grounding and new knowledge learning, while Qwen3.5-Plus performs best on new information application. We further analyze judge reliability, context length, image count, and representative failure cases. Code is available at https://github.com/IamLihua/CLBench-V.

AI.tldr: CLBench-V is a multimodal context-learning benchmark for evaluating how models ground, apply, and acquire knowledge from multimodal contexts, across science, finance, long documents, spatial reasoning, and web VQA. It reveals that multimodal context learning is not yet saturated (best overall score 0.2847 on 3,443 instances) and identifies model strengths: InternVL3.5-30B-A3B for grounding/knowledge learning and Qwen3.5-Plus for information application, with automated data construction and analysis of failure modes.
